articleTitle: Voltage dividers with low phase angle errors for a wideband power measuring system
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A set of resistive voltage dividers has been designed for low phase angle errors. The dividers were made for a wideband power measuring systems to cover voltages up to 1000 V. The phase angle errors of the dividers have been verified in a step-up procedure using two sampling voltmeters. Except for the highest ranges the phase angle errors are within a few /spl mu/rad at 50 Hz and within /spl plusmn/ 50 /spl mu/rad at 1500 Hz.

articleTitle: On the measurement of stationary electric fields in air
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Applications and measurement methods for field measurements are reviewed. Recent developments using optical technology are examined. The various methods are compared. It is concluded that the best general purpose instrument is the isolated cylindrical field mill, but MEMS technology could furnish better instruments in the future.

articleTitle: Development of a high precision AC standard shunt for AC power measurement
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The authors developed an AC standard shunt (rated 10 A, 0.1 /spl Omega/), for frequencies from DC to 10 kHz, which has a highly stable resistance value and small phase angle error. By using this AC standard shunt, AC power and current may be measured with high accuracy. The stability and uncertainty of the shunt correspond to 3 ppm with regard to AC power measurement at 1 kHz.

articleTitle: Synthesis of precision AC waveforms using a SINIS Josephson junction array
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A synthesizer of precision AC waveforms based on a SINIS Josephson junction array has been developed. The array is divided into 15 segments in a binary series and the segments are individually biased using a high speed bias source with a 100 ns rise time. The design considerations and accuracy limitations of the system are discussed and comparisons between the synthesizer and thermal converters are presented.

articleTitle: Inductance calibration in the frequency range from 50 Hz to 1 MHz at PTB
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Inductance calibrations at PTB are carried out with a Maxwell-Wien bridge. This bridge has the advantage that the first order bridge equation is independent of frequency which means that the bridge has the potential to be operated in a large frequency range. However, the actual frequency range, from power frequencies up to 1 MHz, requires an investigation of higher order effects.

articleTitle: Realization of an atomic microwave power standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We demonstrate the feasibility of a novel microwave power standard based on the electromagnetic interaction with cold atoms. Under the effect of the radiation, the internal state populations will undergo a Rabi oscillation. The measurement of its frequency will allow the determination of the electromagnetic field strength.

articleTitle: Evaluation of uncertainty in AC voltage measurement using a digital voltmeter and Swerlein's algorithm
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A model is proposed for a sampling algorithm that uses a high-resolution voltmeter for measuring the RMS value of a sinusoidal voltage waveform. The uncertainty associated with the result of measurement is evaluated according to the rules in the ISO/BIPM guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement. The standard uncertainty was evaluated to be less than 5/spl times/10/sup -6/ in the 1-1000 V and 1-100 Hz ranges. The uncertainty contribution associated with the conditioner and amplifier frequency response correction is dominant in the high frequency range.

articleTitle: Current transformer calibration using synchronous sampling
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A comparison of current transformers' output current is performed by sampling the output voltage on resistive shunts. The complex current ratio is obtained from sampled data using the 3PSF algorithm. An uncertainty budget is presented for the proposed measurement setup.

articleTitle: FEM analysis of shielding effectiveness of magnetic shield of comparator by ANSYS program
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new method in which ANSYS program is used to calculate the magnetic shield effectiveness of comparator and design the magnetic shield is given. This method has been applied in the heavy current comparator we designed; the result is quite ideal.

articleTitle: A current-comparator-based system for calibration of optical instrument transformers with analog and digital outputs
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. An overview of the development of a system comprising of instruments, based on the current-comparator technology, for calibration of optical instrument transformers with analog and digital outputs is presented. The instruments include a transimpedance amplifier for operation of input currents from 1 A to 10,000 A, a high voltage active divider for operation of input voltages from 1 kV to 500 kV, a current-comparator bridge, and two sampling voltmeters. The current comparator is used in a feedback loop to correct the magnitude and phase of the outputs of the transimpedance amplifier and the high voltage active divider to an accuracy of better than 10 parts per million and 10 /spl mu/rad, respectively. The sampling voltmeters are effectively used as 18-bit A/D converters.

articleTitle: 50 Hz current measurements with Rogowski coils
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The applicability of Rogowski coils for high precision measurements of 50 Hz currents is studied. In the set-up, Rogowski coils serve as current sensors and the amplitude and phase are determined with a sampling voltmeter. Another measurement channel enables current ratio and electrical power measurements. Preliminary expanded uncertainties are of the order of 30 ppm in current and 40 /spl mu/rad in phase.

articleTitle: Excellent charge offset stability in Si-based SET transistors
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have obtained a large improvement in one aspect of the single-electron tunneling (SET) charge offset, Q/sub 0/, problem. The long-term drift of Q/sub 0/ makes it infeasible or impossible to integrate many devices. In contrast to metal-based SET transistors (SETTs), the long-term drift in Si-based SETTs appears to be at least one thousand times smaller (better).

articleTitle: Improved high-current thin-film multijunction thermal converters
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report on the fabrication of new thin-film multijunction thermal converters suitable for the measurement of current and new, simpler multiconverter modules that are much easier to manufacture than previous multiconverter modules.

articleTitle: Improvement of NTP time offset under the asymmetric network with double packets method
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The NTP (Network Time Protocol) is widely used in various networks, such as from LAN to WAN. In the case of Internet, the time synchronization accuracy is degraded due to the property of the asymmetric structure of the network between the NTP server and the client. We propose a new technique to reduce the effect of this problem using double packets method.

articleTitle: Extension of Swerlein's algorithm for AC voltage measurement in the frequency domain
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A sampling algorithm that uses a high-resolution voltmeter for measuring the RMS value of a sinusoidal voltage waveform is presented. The technique is a modification of a previously described approach. In the new approach the RMS values of the specified harmonics are evaluated by a multiple linear regression algorithm.

articleTitle: A current-comparator-based bridge for calibrating power and energy standards at 50/60 Hz
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A power standard for calibrating high-accuracy wattmeters and watt-hour meters at 50/60 Hz is described. The technique is a modification of a previously described approach that utilizes a power bridge based on a current comparator. This standard was used in a recent international comparison of 50/60 Hz power.

articleTitle: A method to determine the low frequency behavior of thermal converters
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A method to determine the low frequency behaviour of thermal converters using a resistor as standard is described. The method has been used to determine the AC-DC transfer difference of multijunction thermal converters and planar multijunction thermal converters in the frequency range 10 Hz to 400 Hz. The results of a comparison agree with predicted values within /spl plusmn/0.5-10/sup -6/.

articleTitle: A new approach to Johnson noise thermometry using a quantum voltage noise source for calibration
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We describe a new approach to Johnson noise thermometry (JNT) that takes advantage of the recent advances in Josephson voltage standards and digital signal processing techniques. Previous attempts at high-precision thermometry using Johnson noise have been limited by the non-ideal performance of the electronic systems. By using the perfect quantization of voltages from the Josephson effect, any arbitrary broadband waveform can be synthesized and used as a calculable noise source for calibrating the cross-correlation electronics. With better calibration, we should be able to achieve relative accuracies of parts in 10/sup 5/ for an arbitrary temperature in the range between 84 K and 430 K. We present the latest measurements of our recently constructed JNT system.

articleTitle: Comparison of the measurement of current transformers: EUROMET projects 473 and 612
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The EUROMET Project 473 "Comparison of the measurement of current transformers" started in April 1999, with eleven European National Measurement Institutes (NMI), and was completed in June 2001. A supplementary comparison Project 612 began in December 2000, with a further four NMIs and is estimated to be completed in April 2002.

articleTitle: Traceable measurements on dielectric reference liquids over the temperature range 10 - 50 /spl deg/C using coaxial-line methods
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A programme of traceable measurements of the complex permittivity of dielectric reference liquids from 30 MHz to 5.0 GHz and 10 - 50 /spl deg/C has been completed and the results have been tabulated in an NPL report. This paper discusses the measurement techniques, which were based on coaxial-lines, and the outcome of the work.

articleTitle: A reference standard system based on DC current
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) particle accelerator project requires an accuracy of /spl sim/10/sup -6/ in the control of the current to the superconducting magnets. A new infrastructure for calibration is being built at CERN based on DC current reference standards rather than voltage. The paper describes the rationale, the infrastructure, the transfer methods and the performance.

articleTitle: New AC current shunts of MIKES
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new construction principle of AC current shunts has been applied to a set of shunts for AC currents from 1 A to 20 A, 20 Hz-10 kHz. The completed set will also cover current ranges from 20 mA to 1 A. The shunts are stable and do not show excessive AC-DC amplitude or phase differences and can thus be calibrated to work as AC current and resistance reference standards up to 10 kHz.

articleTitle: 100 mH travelling standard for the EUROMET 607 pilot intercomparison
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A 100 mH standard inductor has been developed for the EUROMET Project n. 607 "Intercomparison of a 100 mH inductance standard". The standard is thermostated. to 0.01/spl deg/C, and configured as a four-terminal pair standard. First characterization results are shown.

articleTitle: Accurate measurement of complex permittivity of liquids using the in-waveguide technique
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The complex permittivity of a number of liquids has been measured using the in-waveguide technique at the X and Ku band. A particular piece of waveguide is designed for the measurement of liquid materials. A TRL (thru-reflect-line) calibration technique is applied for the calibration of this waveguide system. The measured permittivity results of some liquids such as methanol and propyl alcohol compare well with those measured using an open-ended waveguide technique.

articleTitle: Progress in relating the kilogram to Planck's constant with the NPL Watt balance
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The NPL moving-coil Watt balance has been operated regularly for the last two years. The results exhibit good short-term noise and stability but show two significant drifts over periods of 1 to 4 months. The long-term nature of the drifts has hindered the search for their cause which is now thought to be due to interacting mechanical distortions which alter the alignment of the apparatus after evacuation. Modifications are in hand to eliminate the effects of these distortions.

articleTitle: Measurement of reflection coefficient of RF signal source using a mismatch power meter with loss-less dielectric
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have proposed a method measuring the equivalent reflection coefficient of radio-frequency (RF) broadband signal source in its working condition using a mismatch power meter with loss-less dielectric. Measurement has been made for a signal source of X-band rectangular waveguide.

articleTitle: Calibration for time domain propagation constant measurements on power cables
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A method has been developed for characterising the wave propagation properties of medium voltage (MV) power cables. The technique is based on time and frequency domain analysis of short pulse propagation. Particular attention is paid to the measurement calibration, as samples with arbitrary characteristic impedances cause significant multiple reflections in the test set-up.

articleTitle: Quantum resistance standards with double 2DEG
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new generation of quantum Hall array resistance standards (QHARS) designed from GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures with double two-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs) has been developed. First results of measurements carried out on a single Hall bar (R/sub K//4) and 50 Hall bars placed in parallel by triple connections (R/sub K//200) are presented.

articleTitle: Polyphase synthesizer for unlike-impedance intercomparison system
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The system for four-terminal pair intercomparison of unlike impedances of IEN has now been provided with a new direct-digital synthesis generator, having multiple outputs, isolation among the channels, and high amplitude and frequency stability. Experimental results in the new and old configuration are shown and compared.

articleTitle: A coil-type capacitive sensor for measurement of the deterioration of engine oil
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A' coil-type capacitive sensor that allows the deterioration of car engine to be measured in situ has been developed. The degree of deterioration of the used oil is determined by capacitance measurements.

articleTitle: New generation of quantum Hall array resistance standards
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: New quantum Hall array resistance standards (QHARS) with nominal values ranging from R/sub K//200 to 50R/sub K/ (i=2 plateau) have been developed. First results show that R/sub K//200 (/spl sim/129 /spl Omega/) and 16R/sub K//4130 (/spl sim/100 /spl Omega/) standards have Hall resistances which agree with their nominal values within 5 parts in 10/sup 9/ (1/spl sigma/) when supplied by currents up to 4 mA.

articleTitle: Simulated inductance standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We propose in this paper a technique for emulating standard inductors with a tee network of two resistors and capacitor and with buffer in feedback circuit. Unwanted impedances to ground of the emulating tee network may be canceled by introducing a buffer. We anticipate that inductors for values higher than 1 H can be emulated with accuracy of least 0.01%.

articleTitle: Progress towards NRC's fountain clock FCs1
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. Systematic improvements of NRC's cesium fountain clock prototype have resulted in a stability reaching /spl sigma//sub y/(/spl tau/)=1.5/spl times/10/sup -12/ /spl tau//sup -1/2/, the best ever obtained at NRC for a Cs standard. We are in the process of completing the construction of the cesium fountain clock.

articleTitle: A high precision 24 GHz FMCW-radar based on a fractional-N ramp-PLL
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A 24 GHz FMCW-radar system is presented using a fractional-N phase locked loop ramp generator. This fractional-N ramp generator achieves relative ramp nonlinearities below 10/sup -8/. Among other applications, linear frequency ramps are important tools in high precision FMCW-radar systems. Highly linear frequency ramps make post-measurement error correction feasible. Other important aspects of the high performance FMCW-radar system are the design of the microwave circuit and the digital signal processing of the IF signals.

articleTitle: The influence of hydrogen and nitrogen on the floating zone growth of ultra-pure silicon crystals
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The aim of this paper is to give new informations about our experience concerning the influence of hydrogen on the qualities of dislocation-free FZ silicon and an explanation of the silicon molar volume inconsistency.

articleTitle: Transportable Josephson voltage standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The development of a portable 1-V Josephson voltage standard is described. Its accuracy is the same as that of typical laboratory systems, but its weight and volume allow this equipment to be transported by a single person. The system is intended for comparisons and verifications of laboratory Josephson voltage standards with an uncertainty of less than 1/spl times/10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: Calculable impulse voltage calibrator for calibration of impulse digitizers
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Design and construction of a calibrator for lightning and switching impulse voltage measuring instruments is presented. The operating voltage range is from 50 mV to 300 V. The estimated uncertainty for the peak value is 0.03% and for front time and time to half value less than 1%.

articleTitle: Design of a 10 mA DC current reference standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new DC current reference standard, named the PBC, has been developed for high-current power converter calibration in the LHC project at CERN. This standard provides a near ideal 10 mA DC current with long-term drift of less than 1 ppm/year. The paper describes the requirements and the detailed design of the unit.

articleTitle: The effects of the environmental conditions of some Zener voltage references
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We measured variations of output voltages of four Zener standards (Fluke732B) with change of environmental conditions such as humidity, temperature and pressure. Four Zener standards have negligibly small humidity characteristics. The characteristic of the temperature was the order of 0.01 ppm/K. The characteristic of the pressure was approximately 0.02 ppm/10 hPa.

articleTitle: An automatic measurement apparatus for low value magnetic flux with high resolution
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: When a low value flux is to be measured, the induced signal in the measuring coil would be very weak and the instrument resolution thus becomes very important (Chen Duoxingr, Magnetic field Measurement, Beijing, 1985). Here a nanovoltmeter is used as the preamplifier to detect the induced signal from the measuring coil and is followed by a digital integrator to obtain the flux value. Thus a resolution of less than 1 nWb for flux measurement is attained.

articleTitle: The effectiveness of current-comparator magnetic shields against leakage fields at power frequencies
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A magnetostatic approach is used to identify the relevant parameters for current-comparator magnetic shielding design and to derive simple expressions for the shielding effectiveness against leakage fields generated by ratio windings.

articleTitle: The CERN current calibrator-a new type of instrument
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The LHC accelerator project will require an accuracy of 10/sup -6/ in the control of current to the superconducting magnets. A new infrastructure for high current calibration is being created, based on DC current reference standards. This paper describes the design of a device generating an output current from 0 to /spl plusmn/10 A with the required accuracy.

articleTitle: Realization of metre with femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The measurement of length with the use of the multimode radiation of a stable femtosecond laser makes it possible to measure the length directly using frequency standards that operate from the radio to optical spectral regions. The absolute error of such measurements is the same as for monochromatic emission. In addition, discreteness in the determination of the interferometer length can constitute around a meter or more, which is of special interest for precision measurements of long lengths.

articleTitle: 1:30000 cryogenic current comparator with optimum squid readout
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We developed a 1:30000 Cryogenic Current Comparator for SET current amplification. A dedicated low-noise, directly-coupled SQUID was used for the readout, which allowed reaching a sensitivity close to ideal. The ratio error was <9/spl times/10/sup -9/. The CCC-SQUID equivalent current input noise was 3.0 fA/Hz/sup 1/2/, measured down to 0.1 Hz.

articleTitle: Results of the project "Silicon for Mass Unit and Standard" (SIMUS)
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The structural and stoichiometric characterisations of silicon crystals are reported to find the origin of a molar volume discrepancy. The target of reproducing this anomaly was achieved and an hypothesis is proposed.

articleTitle: A new design for calculable resistor
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: UME has improved a coaxial and bifilar type of resistors that have been widely used for determining of the resistance unit from DC to up to several kHz at many primary laboratories. This paper describes the modeling, construction and measurement results of the calculable resistors, which are specially designed in order to eliminate the effects of vibration and mechanical shocks during transportation, at a nominal value of 1 k/spl Omega/, 10 k/spl Omega/ and 12,906 k/spl Omega/.

articleTitle: Quantum Josephson D/A converter driven by trains of short 2/spl pi/-pulses
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The effects used for quantum Josephson digital-to-analogue (D/A) conversion are discussed. The dynamics of an overdamped Josephson junction (JJ) driven by a series of short 2/spl pi/-pulses of programmable intensity and repetition rate is described. The results are presented both analytically and in graphical form.

articleTitle: Status of the NIST "electronic kilogram" experiment
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has rebuilt the apparatus and facilities for the watt balance experiment. The goal is to electronically monitor the SI kilogram at an uncertainty of 10 nW/W. We discuss the design changes and available test results to illustrate the improvements of the system.

articleTitle: Methods and instrumentation for the characterisation of powerline harmonics analysers
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes new methods developed in VNIIM for the calibration of high accuracy powerline harmonics analysers at lower harmonic ratios. The possibility of measuring ratios of harmonics from 2 to 40 lower than 1% with an absolute uncertainty of less than 0.005% using known and well-characterised instrumentation for the measurement of voltage, current and active power has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: New ultra-sensitive Michelson-Morely experiment
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new Michelson-Morley experiment is proposed by measuring the beat frequency of two near degenerate modes with orthogonal propagation in a single spherical resonator. The unique properties of the experiment allow: 1. Substantial common mode rejection of some noise sources: 2. Simple calculation of the signal if Special Relativity is violated. We show that optimum filtering may be used to increase the signal to noise ratio, and to search for a preferred direction of the speed of light. We conclude that an improvement in sensitivity of order 10/sup 5/ is possible using this technique.

articleTitle: Optimizing the series connection of thermal converters for AC current step-up
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: When comparing AC-DC current differences of thermal converters connected in series, capacitive leakage currents from the interconnecting point to the surroundings, and the heater to thermocouple capacitance can become significant, particularly at high frequencies. A method of optimising the series connection, to reduce the leakage currents to less than 5/spl times/10/sup -6/ relative to the measured current, has been modelled and tested experimentally.

articleTitle: No-load loss measurements of power transformers under distorted supply voltage waveform conditions
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The problem of correcting the results of no-load loss measurements of power transformers for the effect of distorted supply voltage waveform on the magnetic flux in the core and hence on both the hysteresis and eddy current loss components of core losses is presented. The instrumentation requirements for no-load loss measurements to ensure proper application of the correction formula are described.

articleTitle: AC resistance ratio bridge for evaluation of calculable AC/DC resistors
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper summarizes the construction and operation of our quadrifilar resistor and newly developed precision AC resistance ratio bridge with relative uncertainty of about a few parts in 10/sup 8/. The quadrifilar resistor is used as the resistance transfer standard from DC to about 10 kHz frequency range. However, its frequency dependence is usually certified only by calculation based on the Gibbing's theory. We report our plan to evaluate the correctness of calculations by comparing its frequency dependence to that of a bifilar resistor using the AC resistance ratio bridge.

articleTitle: AC Josephson voltage standard error measurements and analysis
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer can be used as a precision voltage source for both AC and DC signals. Recent improvements in circuit designs have resulted in output voltages greater than 100 mV so that we can investigate AC metrology measurements in the frequency range from 1 kHz to 50 kHz. In this paper we present experimental measurements of several significant error sources that must be considered in order to create an intrinsic AC voltage standard at these frequencies. These results and the corresponding theoretical analysis allow us to move toward creating a practical AC Josephson voltage standard.

articleTitle: Pulse width modulation type Josephson AC waveform synthesizer
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The operation principle of a digital-to-analogue conversion (DAC) for an accurate AC waveform synthesis based on a pulse width modulation (PWM) of an output voltage of an overdamped Josephson junction (JJ) array is considered. The PWM of the voltage is achieved by the PWM of a sine microwave JJ array bias at a constant DC bias. A set-up realizing the above method is described. To illustrate the synthesizer operation principle, JJ array I-V curves at two microwave power levels and an example of the PWM voltage signal are shown.

articleTitle: AC-DC voltage transfer at UME
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new AC-DC voltage transfer system has been established at UME. The standards consist of a group of planar multijunction thermal converters (PMJTC), whose basic level (1 V to 3 V) is calibrated in PTB. A new software developed at UME is used for step-up and down procedures in order to establish voltages from 2 mV to 1000 V in the frequency range from 10 Hz to 1 MHz.

articleTitle: High voltage scaling with minimum power corrections
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The design and construction of two high voltage resistive dividers and an associated automated four terminal resistance ratio bridge are described. Together they allow ratio calibration from 10 V to 1200 V without any power coefficient corrections above the 10 V at 10 k/spl Omega/ level. The bridge may also be used for calibration of resistors at relatively high powers.

articleTitle: A measurement system for traceable calibration of power harmonics and flicker analysers
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes a precision measurement system developed at NML for traceable calibration of three-phase instruments measuring harmonics of current up to 16 A, voltage fluctuation and flicker. Current and voltage harmonics up to the 99/sup th/ and fluctuating voltages can be generated and measured with relative uncertainties close to 1/spl times/10/sup -5/.

articleTitle: Delay calibration method for precise and accurate two way satellite time and frequency transfer
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The two way satellite time and frequency transfer (TWSTFT) is one of the most accurate and precise time transfer techniques. But there are possibilities of nanosecond level time transfer errors due to delay variations, mainly caused by temperature variations. This paper reports a measurement technique under development at the Communications Research Laboratory using a multi-channel time transfer modem.

articleTitle: Material characterization using a quasi-optical measurement system
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Application of a quasi-optical apparatus in the determination of the constituent parameters of materials is presented in this paper. Correction terms are introduced to remove the errors due to the misplacement of the sample and the calibration procedure. Good agreement was observed between manufacturer specifications and measurements after application of the correction terms.

articleTitle: Improved SINIS Josephson junction series arrays for the quantum voltmeter
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The quantum voltmeter has been further developed towards a compact and easy-to-use system. Optimised 1 V SINIS series arrays generate steps of constant voltage whose width exceeds 1 mA. A new and improved design for 10 V arrays is under development, with the investigations described here serving as a basis.

articleTitle: Characterization of instrument transformers with nonsinusoidal waveforms
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We introduced a decomposition of the error of measuring transformers with focus on their characterization for the measurement of power under nonsinusoidal conditions. Examples of its use in typical cases are presented. A practical implementation of the error definitions is proposed.

articleTitle: High performance mV-amplifier for the planar multijunction thermal converter
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new amplifier concept is developed which combines the conventional master-slave operational amplifier structure and the flying supply technique. The new amplifier is viewed as an input stage for the planar multijunction thermal converter for ac-dc voltage transfer in the mV-range. High input impedance and adjustable ac-dc transfer differences are the main advantages of this design.

articleTitle: High accuracy evaluation of CENAM's primary frequency standard: second order Doppler shift
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The Centro Nacional de Metrologia in Mexico has developed an optically pumped cesium beam frequency standard, the CsOP-1. Currently, the major sources of systematic effects are being analysed and their corresponding frequency shift effects in the CsOp-1. In this work, we re-evaluate the second order Doppler shift by taking into account the modulation parameter.

articleTitle: The European ACQHE project: modular system for the calibration of capacitance standards based on the quantum Hall effect
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Starting in 1998 a project funded by the European Commission has been carried out in a co-operation of seven partners. The aim of this project was to establish a measurement system which allows the calibration of standard capacitors in terms of R/sub K-90/. The whole system comprises suitable quantum Hall samples, an automated bridge system and auxiliary devices to calibrate and characterize the whole set-up. The uncertainty for the calibration of a 10-pF capacitor is about 1 part in 10/sup 7/.

articleTitle: Characterization of 1-10 000 nF capacitance standard for future CCEM key comparison
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The transportable capacitance standard 1 nF-10 /spl mu/F for CCEM key comparison of capacitance is developed. The standard consists of five ceramic dielectric hermetically sealed capacitors with 4 terminal-pair connections. Capacitors are placed into temperature-controlled oven, which maintains a constant (/spl plusmn/0,05/spl deg/C) temperature of about 30/spl deg/C. The long-term measurements have shown that capacitance stability is within the limits of 1-10 ppm per one year, short-term stability is of order of few units of 10/sup -8/.

articleTitle: Resistive transfer standards for transfer of QHR value to 10 kOhm
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Several variants of resistive transfer standard (RTS) for link between quantum Hall resistance (QHR), 12.9 k/spl Omega/ or 6.45 k/spl Omega/, and decimal resistance, 10 k/spl Omega/, are developed and investigated. Relative uncertainty of transition does not exceed (1-3)/spl times/10/sup -8/ under. The main features of the standard are the usage of the minimal number of equal resistors, small (of order 1-20 ppm) deviation of actual transfer coefficient value from nominal value, self-calibration, and simplicity of use.

articleTitle: The development and evaluation of coaxial ac resistors at CSIR-NML
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: CSIR-NML is in the process of developing ac bridges to realize capacitance from a quantum Hall resistance system. This process involves the development of resistors with calculable frequency dependence. We describe the development and evaluation of a calculable coaxial ac resistor that is based on the design by Haddad [1969].

articleTitle: Influence of calibration uncertainties on VNA S-parameter measurements
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: For the widespread 12-term TMSO calibration of 4-sampler vector network analyzers (VNAs), the sensitivity coefficients of the S-parameters of two-ports are derived with respect to the deviations of the reflection coefficients of the one-port calibration standards used. The obtained expressions are suitable for the establishment of the uncertainty budget.

articleTitle: DC conductivity measurements in the Van der Pauw geometry
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Conductivity measurements are an important tool for quality control of aluminum alloys in aircraft manufacture. Industrial measurements using commercial conductivity meters are performed using eddy currents (60 kHz) whereas many conductivity standards are traceable through measurements at DC. A combined project of NPL, PTB, and NMi has been started aiming a.o. at improving the agreement of conductivity measurements with DC and AC methods. In this paper we describe the first results of a new methodology for DC conductivity measurements in the Van der Pauw geometry.

articleTitle: Determining the source match of a generator
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Several methods for determining the equivalent source match of a generator are discussed, with emphasis on the 1 mW 50 MHz reference source of power meters. With relative cheap components reflections below 0.01 can be determined with an uncertainty of the same order of magnitude.

articleTitle: A 10 T/spl Omega/ per step Hamon transfer standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: To evaluate high-resistance measurements and scaling in the range 1 T/spl Omega/ to 100 T/spl Omega/, a 10 T/spl Omega//step Hamon transfer standard is being developed. The design uses fabrication techniques developed in recent years at NIST to construct high-resistance standards.

articleTitle: Intercomparison measurements of direct voltage from 10 kV to 200 kV between NRC, Canada and JEMIC, Japan
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Two 100 kV JEMIC dividers were used as travelling standards in comparison tests against standard dividers maintained at JEMIC and at NRC. The dividers could be used independently or combined to provide a travelling standard rated at 200 kV. The voltage measured by each system is taken as the product of the ratio of that system and the reading on the corresponding multimeter. The difference between the same voltage measured on both systems simultaneously was always less than /spl plusmn/40 /spl mu/V/V.

articleTitle: Analysis of the time constant for the bifilar calculable AC/DC resistors
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The time constant /spl tau/ of the bifilar type calculable AC/DC resistor, with the aim of realizing the standard of the phase angle /spl theta/ (= /spl omega//spl tau/), has been analyzed. From the results of calculations, it has been shown that the geometrical and electrical conditions where the time constant of the resistor becomes zero (/spl tau/ = 0) can be obtained within the proper dimensions.

articleTitle: Statistical uncertainty analysis of CCEM-K2 comparisons of resistance standards
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Details of the statistical uncertainty analysis applied to key comparison CCEM-K2 are reported. Formulas were derived to determine the uncertainty of the combined difference between the measurements of multiple artifacts by an NMI and the corresponding predictions based on pilot lab measurements. In addition, the uncertainties of the reference value of the key comparison and the degrees of equivalence between two NMIs are obtained.

articleTitle: The uncertainty evaluation of automatic direct current comparator bridge
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A practical procedure for ratio measurement uncertainty estimation of auto DCC Bridge is described. By comparison with CCC, the result is confirmed.

articleTitle: Improvements and extensions of high direct voltage measurements at NRC, Canada
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Improvements to the measurement capabilities for high direct voltage at NRC are outlined. Measurements to establish the relative performance of dividers are reported. Initial tests using a null method to compare two measuring systems are described.

articleTitle: Precision measurement with gravity
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. The author describes some of the work directed towards the measurement of G, g, and g/spl mu//spl nu/. A number of recently completed measurements of G have had, and a number of ongoing measurements have, the aim of improving the accuracy of the first of these "gs" from today's 1.5 parts in 10/sup 2/ to better than one part in 10/sup 4/ (to somewhat better than the accuracy with which it was thought to be known 10 years ago). By contrast, our ability to accurately measure the second "g" has, during the past forty years, enjoyed a remarkable 3 orders-of-magnitude improvement. Lastly, sometime in the next decade or so, the final "g" can be expected to provide us with new insights into things such as the formation of massive black holes and galaxy evolution as well as a variety of other objects of astrophysical interest. The role of precision measurement science in carrying out these measurements, and, indeed, in underpinning all of scientific progress, is highlighted. Finally, the commonality of these three different measurements is pointed out.

articleTitle: Directive wideband TEM horn antenna for precise free-space measurements
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An optimization process is employed to design a broadband directive TEM horn. The antenna is fed through a tapered balun, which maintains the horn bandwidth and improves its radiation pattern. A dielectric material loads the whole ensemble so that the system becomes small and well-supported. This antenna with such characteristics is appropriate for precise free-space measurements of the reflection coefficient.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Newtonian gravitational constant G
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present latest results for the Wuppertal gravitational experiment which is based on a microwave resonator. The gravitational force of two test masses acting on the resonator is measured as a function of distance. After more than a year of data taking, we present the results.

articleTitle: Towards quantum AC voltage standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have studied the possibility of realizing AC voltages with metrological accuracy. In this paper we propose two experimental setups for generating accurate sinusoidal voltage waveforms from square-wave biased nonhysteretic programmable Josephson array voltage standards.

articleTitle: Optical frequency standards based on a cooled strontium ion
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An optical frequency standard, based on the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ transition in 674 nm in /sup 88/Sr/sup +/, has been characterized and the frequency measured with a femtosecond laser comb. Progress on developing a standard based on /sup 87/Sr/sup +/ will also be reported.

articleTitle: Measurements of a high-Q TE/sub 0,1,/spl delta// frequency-temperature compensated sapphire Bragg distributed resonator
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A TE/sub 01/spl delta// 9.00 GHz sapphire resonator was constructed with sapphire and rutile supports designed to act as a Bragg distributed resonator (patent pending) to reduce cavity losses. The amount of rutile was chosen using FEM to annul the temperature coefficient of frequency. Here we confirm the resonator to have an annulment temperature of -7.8/spl deg/C and Q-factor of 65,000 limited by the dielectric loss tangent.

articleTitle: Voltage waveform synthesizer based on Josephson array chip with binary subdivisions
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper we describe an AC waveform synthesizer based on an overdamped Josephson junction (JJ) array with binary subdivided sections. We used a 10 GHz 8-bit SINIS JJ array chip manufactured by PTB. We developed the software to drive the synthesizer. Preliminary results of synthesis-measurement type experiments are presented in both graphical and table forms.

articleTitle: Calibration of capacitance and dissipation factor bridges
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new method is presented for the calibration of capacitance and dissipation factor bridges. These bridges form the values indicated by them from the complex ratio of their input currents. For calibration, two sinusoidal AC currents are synthesized with the aid of a digital, programmable two-channel AC voltage source and two AC resistors and fed into the bridge. The complex ratio of these synthesized input currents is calculated from the AC voltage ratio determined by a sampling method, and from the impedance ratio of the AC resistors. At currents of about 5 mA, their ratio at frequencies of about 50/60 Hz can be exactly realized and measured with uncertainties of less than 1/spl times/10/sup -6/ or 1 /spl mu/rad.

articleTitle: A current-comparator technique for measuring harmonic distortion of the loss current in high voltage cable insulation
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Water trees, a type of deterioration that develops in high voltage cable insulation in a humid environment, introduce harmonic distortion in the waveform of the loss current component of the capacitive current of cable insulation. The measurements of the total harmonic distortion could be used as a diagnostic tool to assess the operating conditions of power cables, in particular polymeric-type cables, and their remaining insulation life. A current-comparator technique to accurately measure the total harmonic distortion, including test results obtained on laboratory-aged specimens and short lengths of field-aged cables containing water trees, is presented.

articleTitle: An AC Josephson source for Johnson noise thermometry
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have adapted the Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer to create a quantized voltage noise source suitable for calibrating the cross-correlation electronics of a Johnson noise thermometer system. The requirements of long term stability and low voltage amplitude allow dramatic simplification of the bias electronics compared to previous circuits. We describe the bias technique and the superconducting integrated circuit used to generate the pseudo-noise waveforms.

articleTitle: Susceptibility measurement of FM/AM receiver in GTEM-cell
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper, the susceptibility measurement of a common FM/AM receiver is carried out. A brief description of the GTEM-cell is given, as well as EMC measurements, namely susceptibility. The measurement setup and measurement results are shown. The influence of the ambient field to the sensitivity of the receiver was tested.

articleTitle: Lattice spacing mapping in large silicon ingot using high resolution lattice comparator
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Highly pure silicon crystal is used to determine the Avogadro constant through the XRCD method (K. Fujii et al, Metrologia (France), vol. 36, no. 5, pp. 455-64, 1999). In the method, unit cell volume and molar volume has to be measured using standard samples made from an ingot. In this paper, a method of fast lattice spacing mapping in large silicon crystals is described. Resolution of 0.02 ppm is obtained with a measuring time of 5 minutes per point. Measuring time reduction is estimated to be feasible by simple modification of the measurement. The efficacy of this method is discussed.

articleTitle: Type B uncertainty evaluation of IEN CSF1 primary frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report the first accuracy evaluation of the new IEN Cs fountain primary frequency standard. Although preliminary, and performed in absence of a resident H-maser, all the principal effects are evaluated at few units of 10/sup -15/ level. Differential measurements and TWSTFT remote comparisons were used to supply in the absence of the H-maser.

articleTitle: Micromachined thin-film multijunction thermal converters developed at KRISS
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Micromachined thin-film multijunction thermal converters (MJTCs) suitable as high performance ac-dc transfer standards have been fabricated and studied at KRISS. This paper describes their thermal design and the materials chosen to improve performance. And finally performance data are given over a wide range of frequencies and conditions.

articleTitle: Nano-scale integrity and coherence of the S.I
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Traceable measurements at the nano-scale are usually made by establishing links to the scale of the S.I. base units all of which are defined at the macro-scale. We report the results of a study into the implications of the burgeoning developments in nano-technology on the realisation of S.I. quantities at the nano-scale.

articleTitle: Time comparison experiments using Trimble 4700 GPS geodetic receiver
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes tests of precision time transfer using GPS carrier phases. Time comparison experiments were conducted by using a Trimble 4700 geodetic receiver. The internal 10 MHz oscillator of the receiver is disconnected and driven from a hydrogen maser. Time transfer measurements for zero baseline and short baseline were carried out for evaluating the performance of time transfer using the geodetic receiver and applied to the comparison of frequency standards. The results of the time comparison using the receiver has shown that the precision is less than a hundred picosecond. The receiver can be used as a precision time transfer receiver using GPS carrier phases with a longer baseline.

articleTitle: High-frequency thin-film multijunction thermal converter on a quartz crystal chip
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The design of a new planar or thin-film multijunction thermal converter (PMJTC) on a quartz chip results in improved performance for frequencies higher than 100 kHz due to smaller dielectric losses and higher insulation resistance in the quartz membrane and the quartz chip. The window with the membrane is anisotropically etched into the quartz crystal chip. The temperature of the heater is radiometrically sensed with a thin-film infrared sensor. At frequencies higher than 100 kHz the ac-dc voltage transfer differences are one order smaller than with the standard PMJTC with the Si/sub 3/N/sub 4//SiO/sub 2//Si/sub 3/N/sub 4/ sandwich membrane on a silicon chip.

articleTitle: Preliminary evaluation of the Cs atomic fountain frequency standard at NMIJ/AIST
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The National Metrology Institute of Japan has started evaluation of the cesium atomic fountain frequency standard (JF-1) with the purpose of realization of the SI-second. We present preliminary results of the stability measurements and the accuracy evaluation.

articleTitle: DC voltage calibrator based on an array of high-temperature superconductor Josephson junctions
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We are using a quantum DC voltage generated on an array of high-temperature superconductor (HTS) junctions in the developed voltage calibrator with an output voltage up to 10 V. The described concept and the demonstrated parameters of the main parts of the instrument show that the measurement uncertainty of the output voltage will be a few parts in 10/sup 8/.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of the quantum Hall devices
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Quantum Hall resistance has been adopted as an international resistance standard since 1990. GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures grown by molecular beam epitaxy were fabricated into quantum Hall devices. Ten devices with good accuracy were obtained. The effects of temperature, current, and sample homogeneity on the quantum Hall plateau are reported.

articleTitle: A three-phase energy standard at NIM
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A three-phase energy standard has been built at NIM with uncertainty of 30 parts in 10/sup 6/. The system and its uncertainty are reported.

articleTitle: Optimisation of a potentiometric measurement system by calculation of the Allan variance
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A potentiometric measurement system used to compare the quantised Hall resistance with a nominally equal standard resistor and making use of Zener current and compensation voltage sources was studied, to detect the noise limits and optimise the measurement strategy. The Allan variance was used to evaluate the time correlation of repeated measurements.

articleTitle: A compact external-cavity diode laser with a littman configuration
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have constructed a compact extemal-cavity diode laser (ECDL) based on a Limnan configuration with a robust structure of cavity. The laser system offers up to 9-GHz continuous tuning using PZT only. The linewidth of 200 kHz is obtained from beat-note spectrum of two ECDLs.

articleTitle: Study of the limitations of quantized acoustic current devices at PTB and NPL
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present a quantitative comparison between surface acoustic wave devices produced at PTB and Cambridge University. From the temperature dependence of the acoustic current, information on a number of device parameters such as the electron temperature and self-heating can be deduced. The results of this study will be discussed with respect to the limitations they place on the accuracy of the quantized acoustic current (QAC).

articleTitle: A new, larger cryogenic capacitor, and a direct comparison to the calculable capacitor
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A key element of the Electron-Counting Capacitance Standard (ECCS) is the cryogenic capacitor, C/sub cryo/. We report on a new version of C/sub cryo/ which has a value of 10 pF, ten times larger than previous versions. We also report on a new way to compare C/sub cryo/ to the calculable capacitor, C/sub calc/ which does not require tuning C/sub cryo/.

articleTitle: Optical frequency measurements at the National Research Council
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Experiments are described in which a conventional infrared frequency chain is used to measure the frequency of stable laser sources at 10.4 /spl mu/m and 1.5 /spl mu/m. Details are given of a femtosecond frequency comb, which will eventually replace the infrared chain.

articleTitle: Experimental sampling distributions of the Allan variance in DC electrical measurements
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Stochastic serial correlations in DC measurements can be characterized using the Allan variance. Indeed, the Allan variance can be used to characterize the stability of instruments themselves. For such applications it is useful to be able to specify its uncertainty. By repeating sets of 2048 observations more than 500 times in succession, the experimental sampling distribution of the Allan variance was obtained and found to agree well with the chi-square distribution calculated from the number of degrees of freedom estimated from the data.

articleTitle: A new microcalorimeter for measurements in 3.5 mm coaxial line
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new microcalorimeter has been designed and realized for implementing the national power standard up to the frequency of 26.5 GHz at IEN Galileo Ferraris. It is a dry microcalorimeter, incorporating some new refinements that improve the global performances of the measurement system. This microcalorimeter has been originally designed for calibrating classic thermistor mounts fitted with PC 3.5-mm connector, but will be optimized for thermocouple power sensors, which can operate from direct current to 26.5 GHz.

articleTitle: The modification of direct current comparator to extend range up
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A commercial DCC bridge is modified to extend resistance measurement to higher than 1 k/spl Omega/ by changing the track point and driven by a single voltage source. The measurement result shows an uncertainty of ratio within 0.1 to 1.5 parts in 10/sup 6/.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilized 1.54 /spl mu/m Er-Yb bulk laser against sub-Doppler /sup 13/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ absorption lines
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We developed a new compact and massive bulk Er-Yb laser and locked its emission wavelength to various lines of the /sup 13/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ (/spl nu//sub 1/+/spl nu//sub 3/) rovibrational transition at around 1.54 /spl mu/m. Peak to peak frequency stability of the locked laser was /spl plusmn/40 kHz over an observation time of 500 s.

articleTitle: The multiple-N-method for the calibration of vector network analyzer
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The multiple-N-method is a new self-calibration technique for vector network analyzers. N represents a reciprocal, reflection symmetrical network. In contrast to the TRL-method (Through Reflect Line), the calibration circuits of the multiple-N-method are of equal length. Like the TRL-method, the multiple-N-method only needs three calibration circuits.

articleTitle: Proposal of multiple frequency references centered at 1550 nm based on a frequency comb generated from a mode-locked semiconductor laser with a saturable absorber
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We propose an experimental setup for generating multiple frequency references in the optical telecommunication frequency range. It is based on a comb of equally spaced frequencies, centered at 1550 nm, generated by a passively mode-locked semiconductor laser with a saturable absorber. The repetition rate of the pulse train can be modified using a temporal self-imaging technique.

articleTitle: Report on CCEM-K2 comparison of 10 M/spl Omega/ and 1 G/spl Omega/ resistance standards
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An international comparison of DC resistance at 10 M/spl Omega/ and 1 G/spl Omega/ was organized under the auspices of the Comite Consultatif d'Electricite et Magnetisme (CCEM) and piloted by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) with 14 other national metrology institutes (NMIs) participating. Results from the comparison are reported.

articleTitle: Key comparisons for dummies: lessons learned
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper will discuss some of the challenges encountered during a recent key comparison. From these experiences, general lessons will be drawn that should prove useful both for the consultative committees and for future pilot laboratories as they consider organization of future key comparisons.

articleTitle: New Schottky diodes with very broad frequency band
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present a new Schottky diode devise that can be used as ultra-high speed heterodyne receivers, in order to detect mixing signals up to 1 THz. Preliminary results demonstrate a good detection efficiency.

articleTitle: An in-phase and quadrature current separated phantom-burden power source
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new concept for a phantom-burden power source is proposed. The reference power consisting of a pure sinusoidal voltage and an in-phase current is applied to the standard power meter, and the test power of the same voltage and a quadrature current superimposed on the inphase current is applied to the test meter.

articleTitle: Optical photo-detector AC response in the microwave range
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Limitations to a novel method which permits simple and robust determination of the AC response of fast photo-detectors (frequency range > GHz), based on measuring optical RIN and shot noise, are investigated. Particular emphasis is placed on the effects of phase noise.

articleTitle: Resistance scaling from 10 m/spl Omega/ to 10 k/spl Omega/ at MIKES with Cryogenic Current Comparator and Guildline bridges
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An automated measurement system for resistance scaling is developed in MIKES. The system was compared with our Cryogenic Current Comparator (CCC) resistance bridge. The results of the measurements in the range 1 Ohm-10 kOhm agreed within 0.03 ppm. The same CCC bridge is used for the measurements of the 10 mOhm resistor with a combined standard uncertainty less than 1 ppm. Temperature hysteresis was observed in some of the standard resistors during measurements of their temperature coefficients.

articleTitle: New results in optical frequency measurement using a femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report recent results obtained at the BNM-LPTF with the new frequency measurement chain based on a femtosecond laser. An I/sub 2/ stabilized Nd:YAG optical frequency standard, developed at the BNM-INM as a national standard for the "mise en pratique" of the definition of the meter has been measured for the first time.

articleTitle: Coupled microwave resonators as a basis for sensitive bolometric detection
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Describes a novel form of bolometric detector which may have widespread application wherever sensitive measurement of the energy absorbed by the impact of particles is required, whether they be massive particles, photons or even phonons.

articleTitle: A measurement of the gravitational constant using a cryogenic torsion pendulum
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Final analysis is in progress of a measurement of G made using a cryogenic torsion pendulum in the 'dynamic' (time-of-swing) mode. We have collected and analyzed data which will yield a G measurement with about 20 ppm statistical uncertainty. A value for G will be reported at CPEM 2002.

articleTitle: Absolute frequencies, linewidths, and hyperfine structures of iodine transitions near the dissociation limit (523 to 498 nm)
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A widely tunable and high-resolution spectrometer based on a frequency doubled Ti:sapphire laser is used to explore sub-Doppler transitions of iodine molecules in the wavelength range of 523-498 nm. The wavelength-dependence of the hyperfine transition linewidth of iodine is mapped out in this region. Towards the dissociation limit near 500 nm, the hyperfine-resolved patterns are found to be largely modified. A femtosecond optical comb is used to determine the absolute frequency of the 514.7 nm optical standard with more than a 100-fold improvement in precision.

articleTitle: 22 years of quantum Hall effect metrology
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. This talk will be a review of the history of quantum Hall effect metrology from a personal point of view since I had the chance to participate in this history from the beginning. At CPEM 80 von Klitzing introduced his discovery to the metrological community. The question arose, if there is a possible metrological application. Consequently in the early eighties a lot of effort was put into the availability of suitable samples and into experiments, which had been characterized mainly by decreasing the measurement uncertainty, by the search for the best values for the characteristic constant and by clarifying if it might be possible to detect any deviation from the quantization. It was the time when the international co-operation between the metrological institutes in this field started to become very intensive. At the CPEM held in Tsukuba in 1988 a working group of the CCE reviewed critically the experiments available at that time and stated a draft for a recommendation to applicate the quantum Hall effect for the maintenance of the ohm. Through the official bodies of the metre convention this recommendation became effective on January 1st, 1990. All national metrological institutes follow this recommendation since that date. In the meantime this procedure has been established very successfully. The BIPM has built a transportable quantum Hall effect measurement system and has performed up to now at several NMIs bilateral comparisons in calibrating resistances. They show that the results in the calibrations do not differ more than the uncertainties of the set-ups, which have reached a few parts in a billion. Stimulated by this great success in the maintenance of the ohm the desire among metrologists is great to develop a similar procedure for the maintenance of an ac quantity, the farad. Therefore a great effort is put at several institutes into the experimental investigation of the quantum Hall effect with alternating currents in the kHz range. Although the experimental effort is much higher compared to dc measurements, the results indicate that a similar application will be possible.

articleTitle: Nonlinear spectroscopy in an active interferometer with saturable absorber
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The investigation into the form of nonlinear optical resonances in an active Fabry-Perot interferometer with amplifying and absorbing media saturated by an external laser radiation was performed. Such an active interferometer may ensure an enhancement in the intensity of resonances by one order of magnitude as compared with a similar passive system.

articleTitle: An accurate optical frequency measurement system at telecommunication region
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We are now developing an accurate optical frequency measurement system at the telecommunication region using an optical frequency standard with Doppler-free acetylene absorption and a mode-locked fiber laser.

articleTitle: Calibration of 1 Ohm based on a QHR standard using a commercial DCC bridge
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A calibration technique of 1 0 based on a QfR standard(i4 step) using a commercial DCC bridge have been described. Sample characterizations and bridge ratios have been measured using the DCC bridge without a CCC bridge and total combined uncertainty is estimated as about O.lxlOd level.

articleTitle: The BIPM laser standards at 633 nm and 532 nm simultaneously linked to the SI second using a femtosecond laser in an optical clock configuration
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The study of an optical clock based on an iodine-stabilized Nd:YAG laser has been performed using a femtosecond laser. The optical frequency of the iodine-stabilized He-Ne laser at 633 nm and the Nd:YAG laser at 532 nm have been measured simultaneously with a relative uncertainty below 1/spl times/10/sup -12/.

articleTitle: An inductive voltage calibration system based on bootstrapping method
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The need of calibrated inductive voltage dividers (IVD) with the smallest possible uncertainties was appeared for determination, maintenance and dissemination of the ohm and the farad in audio frequencies. In this paper an IVD calibration system that is based on bootstrapping method is described and the preliminary results and improvement efforts are mentioned. The relative uncertainty of the system from the preliminary results is 2.10/sup -8/ for the inphase component, 5.10/sup -8/ for the quadrate component at 1 kHz.

articleTitle: A new determination of the Newtonian gravitational constant at MSL
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes a new determination of the Newtonian gravitational constant, G. Since our last compensated measurement of G, modifications have been made to the apparatus and operating procedures to further identify possible measurement errors and improve the uncertainty. Our latest value and its uncertainty is presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Optical frequency standards based on the /sup 199/Hg/sup +/ ion
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The feasibility of an optical frequency standard based on a /sup 199/Hg/sup +/ ion is discussed. A fractional frequency instability of 7 /spl times/ 10/sup -15/ (at 1 s) has been realized for a laser locked to the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ electric-quadrupole transition at 282 nm (f/sub o/ /spl ap/ 1.06 /spl times/ 10/sup 15/ Hz). The apparatus for a full systematic evaluation using two Hg/sup +/ standards is under construction.

articleTitle: A measurement system for the dissemination of Josephson AC-DC transfer standards
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes a new measurement system for the comparison of alternating voltage standards based on the Josephson effect with those of thermal voltage converters. Target uncertainty is of the order of 1/spl times/10/sup -7/ at frequencies up to 10 kHz.

articleTitle: HTS cryogenic current comparator for non-invasive sensing of charged particle beams
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The principle of the superconducting cryogenic direct-current comparator (CCC) is applied to the non-invasive sensing of charged-particle beams (ions, electrons). We have developed a novel current concentrating technique using HTS thick film material, to increase the sensitivity of the CCC. Recent simulations and experimental measurements of a prototype HTS-CCC operating at 77 K are described.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation in highly birefringent photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report on the influence of pump laser polarization and wavelength on the supercontinuum generated in a highly birefringent photonic crystal fiber. We were able to produce a continuum that extends from 400 to 1700 nm. It can be used, e.g., for optical frequency synthesis.

articleTitle: Optical frequency standard at 1.3 /spl mu/m and 659 nm based on an iodine-stabilized Nd:YAG laser
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A 1319-nm Nd:YAG laser is frequency-stabilized by locking the frequency-doubled output (659 nm) to the Doppler-free absorption lines of molecular iodine. We measure the absolute frequency, and evaluate the stability and reproducibility of the frequency-stabilized laser by using a femtosecond (fs) comb that is phase coherently connected to Cs clocks at NMIJ/AIST.

articleTitle: The coherent population trapping passive frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Coherent population trapping in alkali atoms has opened a new avenue in the implementation of atomic frequency standards having promising characteristics for field use. The paper reviews the state of the art in this subject and describes recent results obtained in the case of a passive Rb standard implemented using such an approach.

articleTitle: An experiment for verification of auxiliary transmission line method to evaluate a microwave thermal noise source
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In order to verify the usefulness of an auxiliary transmission line method, which we have already proposed to evaluate the noise temperature of a microwave thermal noise source, a liquid nitrogen cooled coaxial noise source system has been constructed and its preliminary experiment has been conducted. Then, this measurement result and a result calibrated to the noise source with two known standards have been compared.

articleTitle: Cold atom clocks: status, applications, and perspectives
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. The ability to cool neutral atoms and trapped ions using laser light has brought a new generation of ultra-stable clocks to existence in the microwave and optical domains. The author introduces the basic concepts, and discuss the main factors contributing to the frequency stability and accuracy of these frequency standards. Some applications are presented of these ultra-stable clocks in fundamental physics such as the search for a possible drift of fundamental constants, tests of general relativity and comparison of distant clocks. The possibility of comparing clocks in various parts of the electromagnetic spectrum using mode-locked femtosecond lasers will lead to dramatic advances in the sensitivity of these tests. The interest in the space environment for cold atom experiments is outlined. Thanks to the reduced gravity in an Earth orbiting satellite, interaction times in the clock can significantly exceed that of fountain clocks on the Earth. Several space missions carrying laser cooled cesium and rubidium clocks as well as hydrogen masers are under development for flying onboard the International Space Station in 2006-2007.

articleTitle: Long term stability of TESLA fused silica 10 pF standards
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
