abstract: In this paper we describe stability and other parameters of Czech-made 10 pF fused silica capacitors after 30 years of use. These capacitors were made from three types of fused silica and with different technologies.

articleTitle: Precise dielectric measurement of low loss materials at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The permittivity and loss-tangent of a number of low-loss materials have been measured using the open-resonator system by two methods - the full cavity-length variation technique and the frequency variation technique. While excellent agreement and consistency in results were obtained by both methods, the measured results showed that the cavity-length technique is a little more accurate with a less-noise resonance peak profile. An extensive error analysis is made for the first time for various open resonator measurement methods for a number of specimens of different thickness.

articleTitle: Fast reversed DC measurements using a NbN/TiN/NbN Josephson junction array
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Fast-reversed DC (FRDC) measurements were performed using a NbN/TiN/NbN Josephson junction array developed at AIST. The Josephson junction array was utilized as an auxiliary voltage-stabilizer for a conventional semiconductor FRDC source. The FRDC-DC difference of a thermal converter was measured either with or without the use of the Josephson voltage-stabilizer. The level of agreement between the two configurations was measured to be better than 1 part in 10/sup 7/.

articleTitle: A compact CH/sub 4/-stabilized He-Ne laser with a telescopic cavity
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. A transportable He-Ne/CH/sub 4/ frequency standard based on an original telescopic cavity with a low influence of angular misalignment of mirrors on the laser radiation power has been created. Frequency shifts for various parameters, stability and reproducibility were measured.

articleTitle: A Ca optical frequency standard based on ultra-cold atoms
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: With recently developed strategies to reduce frequency offsets due to residual first-order Doppler effects the relative uncertainty of the Ca optical frequency standard at PTB was reduced to 2.7-10/sup -14/. The weighted mean of the optical frequency measured by a harmonic frequency chain and recently by a femtosecond laser comb is (455 986 240 494 154 /spl plusmn/ 13) Hz. The use of ultra-cold atoms prepared by a novel two-stage cooling method will allow to further reduce frequency offsets.

articleTitle: Characterisation of binary Josephson series arrays of different types at BNM-LNE and comparisons with conventional SIS arrays
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Three 1 V binary Josephson arrays developed by the NIST, the PTB and the VTT and using respectively SNS (superconductor-normal-superconductor), SINIS (superconductor-insulator-normal-insulator-superconductor) and externally shunted SIS (superconductor-insulator-superconductor) junctions have been tested at BNM-LNE. Preliminary results of direct comparisons with conventional SIS arrays globally show a good agreement of less than 0.5 nV, at any nominal voltages between 41 mV and 1.3 V.

articleTitle: Use of the Allan deviation and linear prediction for the determination of the uncertainty on timescale predictions involved in time and frequency calibrations
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The Allan deviation is a statistical tool that has been used extensively in the field of time and frequency for the characterization of the frequency instabilities of oscillators. In this paper a simple prediction algorithm and the Allan deviation are used to determine the uncertainty on the timescale predictions involved in calibration procedures performed in T and F metrology laboratories. This approach can be used to clarify questions about the uncertainty on measurements in T and F but also in other fields of metrology whenever the measured quantity is affected by non-stationary noise.

articleTitle: High precision RF linearizer by digital predistortion technique
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a new adaptive digital predistortion linearization technique and algorithm for high linearity RF power amplifier used for transmitters of IMT-2000 band mobile communication base station. Simulation results show an improvement of -63 dB for the third-order intermodulation distortion suppression. This technique is easy to realize adaptive control and suitable for circuit integration.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic compatibility in platinum resistance thermometers
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The most precise measurement technique for temperature measurements involves platinum resistance thermometers. In order to perform low uncertainty measurements, it is of paramount importance to ensure the electromagnetic compatibility of such thermometers and the rest of the equipment commonly found in a calibration laboratory (namely furnaces, liquid baths and computers).

articleTitle: Development of a silver atom optical clock
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. We are developing an optical frequency standard based on the narrow 4d/sup 10/ 5s /sup 2/S/sub 1/2//spl rarr/4d/sup 9/ 5s/sup 2/ /sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ transition in atomic silver. We have realized a two-photon spectrometer and are now engaged in a measurement of the frequency of the broader but easier-to-detect two-photon transition to the 4d/sup 9/ 5s/sup 2/ /sup 2/D/sub 3/2/ level.

articleTitle: Characteristics of binary Josephson arrays for a programmable voltage standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Within the Euromet project no. 626, I-V curves of two non-hysteretic Josephson arrays (of SINIS and externally shunted SIS types) are studied at NMi as a function of microwave power at the drive frequency of 76.275 GHz and temperature 4 K. A stable operation at about 1.1 V is registered.

articleTitle: Interferometric determinations of the volume of silicon spheres with a direct optical frequency tuning system
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: For accurate volume measurements of 1-kg silicon spheres, a new interferometer with a direct optical frequency tuning system using a phase-lock loop offset locking has been developed. Accurate frequency changes in a laser produced by the frequency tuning system have been used for diameter measurements of the spheres by phase-shifting interferometry.

articleTitle: Isotopically enriched silicon: the atomic path to the kilogram?
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Progress in the experiments for the redefinition of the unit of mass by the X-ray crystal density method is hampered mainly by the insufficient accuracy of silicon molar mass. This paper reports on considerations to calibrate prompt (n,/spl gamma/) spectrometry against data obtained by mass spectrometry. When natural silicon, where df/spl ap/10/sup -6/ is known from mass spectroscopy, is compared with isotopically enriched silicon, two difficulties are overcome: (a) the cross sections etc. cancel out, and (b) the gain in isotopic enrichment is roughly valid for df, too. So, from df=10/sup -6/ we end up with df=6.3/spl times/10/sup -8/ for f/spl ges/0.9995. This material then is used for the fabrication of the 1 kg sphere on which the density and the lattice constant are determined.

articleTitle: Attenuation measurement system in frequency range of 10-100 MHz
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An attenuation measurement system, which employs a traceable inductive voltage divider (IVD) at 1 kHz as a reference standard and the dual channel intermediate frequency (IF) substitution method, is developed for an attenuation standard in the frequency range of 10-100 MHz. The basic properties of the system were experimentally investigated at a frequency of 60 MHz.

articleTitle: Simple atoms, and fundamental constants
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Several applications of simple atoms to precise determination of fundamental constants are considered. We pay a special attention to QED related constants such as the Rydberg constant, the fine structure constant, the muon-to-electron and proton-to-electron mass ratios.

articleTitle: A juggling fountain clock and distributed cavity phase shifts
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have demonstrated a juggling /sup 87/Rb fountain clock. The juggling frequency shift is a particularly interesting measurement. We expect to report measurements of the Ramsey fringe contrast and a comparison to calculations that include photon recoils. We will also present results of calculations of distributed cavity phase shifts.

articleTitle: New technique for microwave characterization of material under compressive stress
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: To investigate the high frequency properties of ferrite materials under stress, a new reflection/transmission cell is designed. A uniaxial compressive stress is applied along a hollow cylinder type sample inserted in a modified coaxial cell. This setup allows measurement of permittivity and permeability under stress (values up to 30 MPa) from 150 MHz up to 10 GHz. Specific calculations are used to take into account the modifications in the line geometry. Accuracy of the measurement method is then evaluated.

articleTitle: A simple and accurate checking method of the DVM performance
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A simple and accurate method to check the performance of an 8.5-digit digital voltmeter with high accuracy (/spl sim/1 pm) is proposed. It is demonstrated that this method is useful to check if such a digital voltmeter is working within the specification given in the catalogue or manual.

articleTitle: Correction of the residual amplitude modulation in FM spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The distortion induced by the residual amplitude modulation in FM spectroscopy is studied and a narrowband rejection technique for the suppression of the amplitude modulation is presented.

articleTitle: Fundamental tests of relativity using cryogenic optical resonators
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report on a new generation of relativity tests. By frequency comparisons utilizing cryogenic optical resonators (COREs), we confirmed (i) the velocity-independence of the speed of light to a threefold higher accuracy, (ii) local position invariance, and (iii) isotropy of space, with an accuracy 3 times better than the best previous experiment.

articleTitle: The NIST microforce realization and measurement project
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has launched a five-year Micro-force Realization and Measurement project focusing on the development of an instrument and laboratory capable of realizing and measuring the SI unit of force below 5/spl times/10/sup -6/ N using the electrical units as the link to the SI.

articleTitle: Frequency band requirements for a precision RMS measurement system based on successive extractions of the means of absolute values
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper investigates the frequency band requirements for the circuits to be used in the implementation of a precision RMS measurement system based on the method of successive extractions of the means of the absolute value signals. The circuits cover a frequency range of 10 Hz to 100 Hz.

articleTitle: Flotation measurements to reveal the reason for the discrepancy in the molar volume of silicon
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Silicon single crystals are used to determine the Avogadro constant on the basis of the ratio of molar volume and atomic volume. To reveal the reason for the discrepancy in the molar volume of silicon found in crystals of different origin, the densities of crystals grown under different conditions were compared using a flotation method. The method and the results obtained are reported and the uncertainty is discussed.

articleTitle: A web-based database of information relating to the evaluation of the Avogadro constant using the XRCD method
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A number of laboratories are working towards an evaluation of the Avogadro constant with combined relative uncertainty of 1 in 10/sup 8/. This will enable a definition of the kilogram based on a specific number of /sup 12/C atoms rather than an artefact based definition. In order to coordinate the data obtained by the participating laboratories, a web-based database has been set up. This database forms part of the BIPM website, although access is limited to participants.

articleTitle: The magnetic moment of the helion in Bohr magnetons
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have previously described an experiment to measure the magnetic moment of the helion in Bohr magnetons. We now have preliminary results using the first of two proposed methods, an irreversible seal-breaking method. Improvements obtainable with the second method are discussed.

articleTitle: An isotropic sensor for the measurement of low frequency electric and magnetic fields
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The theoretical analysis and preliminary measurements shows the possibility of isotropic measurement both of the electric field and of the magnetic field by using a single probe. The solution proposed is a simple one, and makes possible the achievement of an isotropic sensor for determining the electromagnetic interference in the audio frequency band.

articleTitle: Towards an optical measurement of the HFS interval in the 2s state in hydrogen
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We discuss the theoretical status and experimental possibility of an optical determination of the 2s hyperfine interval in atomic hydrogen.

articleTitle: Projecting Zener DC reference performance between calibrations
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Two empirical models are proposed to predict Zener reference standard output voltage based on just 1 or 2 calibration points. The models are derived from a study of 87 Zener standards. The results yield up to a 60% reduction in uncertainty relative to the manufacturer's specification and illustrate the dominance of seasonal effects.

articleTitle: A thermal voltage converter based on thermistors
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents a thermal voltage converter (TVC) using thermistors as temperature detectors instead of thermocouples, as it is commonly used. Thermistors have the advantage of having high temperature coefficients. This permits operation at low working temperatures. In this way, the main causes of AC/DC errors can be reduced.

articleTitle: Scalar Aharonov-Bohm effect on cold atom using a time domain atom interferometer
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The scalar Aharonov-Bohm effect of a time dependent homogeneous magnetic field on neutral cold atoms was demonstrated using a time domain atom interferometer. The interference fringes over the phase shift of more than 200 rad verified the nondispersivity.

articleTitle: A study on the frequency stability of a PLL with GPS signal as input
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The noise characteristics of GPS signals are quite different from that of standard frequency sources. This paper presents the problem of analysing the frequency stability, in particular Allan deviation, and suggests an analytical solution for this problem with a GPS signal as the input of a phase locked loop. This analysis is corroborated by experimental findings.

articleTitle: Direct determination of capacitance standards using a quadrature bridge and a pair of quantised Hall resistors
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We describe measurements made using a quadrature bridge to simultaneously compare two quantum Hall resistors (QHRs) with two 10 nF capacitors at 1233 Hz. This direct approach eliminates uncertainties due to thermal and structural instabilities and to AC/DC differences of the wire resistors normally used with an AC ratio bridge as an intermediary stage.

articleTitle: Digital generator assisted impedance bridge
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A manually-operated prototype wide-range four-terminal-pair universal impedance bridge has been constructed in order to test ideas for an automated bridge. The least relative uncertainty is 2/spl times/10/sup -5/ at 1 kHz and about 20/spl times/10/sup -5/ at 100 kHz. A two-phase digital voltage generator provides convenient sources for the two voltages required to bring the bridge to near but not exact balance. The detector offset voltages are measured with a vector voltmeter and used to correct for the inexact balance.

articleTitle: Precision comparisons and pooled presentations of probability
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Inter-laboratory measurement comparisons can benefit from explicit graphical presentation of their probability density functions (PDFs). It is now as easy to create and manipulate these graphs as it is to use traditional error bars. These graphs improve clarity and generality when discussing uncertainties and their associated assumptions.

articleTitle: An active AC bridge with adaptive current orthogonal decomposition for precision measurement of dielectric loss angle
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: With adaptive orthogonal decomposition of reactive and active current, an active AC bridge, which is implemented by employing analog circuit, is introduced. Its application in measurement of dielectric loss angle for high voltage insulation apparatus can eliminate the effect of harmonics of testing voltage, reduce leakage resistance and capacitance and ease high resolution. Moreover, determination of the reference voltages for orthogonal decomposition and the dynamical characteristics of the bridge are presented.

articleTitle: Comparison of three methods to determine the density of moist air
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Determines the density of air by using the following three methods: CIPM-81/91 formula, air buoyancy artefacts and an optical method. A discrepancy of 10/sup -4/ kg/spl middot/m/sup -3/ was observed between the two absolute methods: the CIPM-81/91 formula and the buoyancy artefacts. Future investigations are underway to clarify this difference.

articleTitle: Counting electrons one by one - overview of a joint European research project
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The European COUNT project exploits two complementary single electron tunneling (SET) devices for use in electrical current metrology: a single electron pump as a current source and a single electron counter as a current meter. Apart from being a quantum current standard, the electron pump could be the basis of a capacitance standard.

articleTitle: An improved sensor for the NIST Cryogenic Thermal Transfer Standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We are developing a new primary standard of ac-dc difference, based on a resistive superconducting transition-edge sensor. We describe the performance limitations of the present device, and present a new sensor design which will improve the operating environment, and hence the performance, of the standard.

articleTitle: Analysis of different measurement set-ups for a programmable Josephson voltage standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Various operational parameters of two different I-V binary programmable Josephson arrays are evaluated and compared within different Josephson array voltage standard (JAVS) set-ups at microwave frequencies around 70 GHz. For this purpose, the investigation of the electrical characteristics of a SINIS-type Josephson array and of an externally shunted SIS-type Josephson array is under way at ten national metrology institutes. The results of the measurements are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: The SCL quantised Hall resistance standard system
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes the quantized Hall resistance standard (QHRS) system established at the SCL. The system is described and measurement results obtained with the system are presented. An uncertainty budget is also presented to show that the system is capable of performing DC resistance measurements from 1 /spl Omega/ to 10 k/spl Omega/ with standard uncertainty of 8 parts in 10/sup 9/.

articleTitle: Probability of pass and probability of fail in pass-or-fail tests
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper the probability of pass (PoP) and the probability of fail (PoF) are derived following a metrological approach, in which concepts such as repeatability, number of effective degrees of freedom, level of confidence, coverage factors and expanded uncertainty will play a role.

articleTitle: Effects of metallic gates on AC quantum Hall measurements
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Using a sample with back-gates, a linear frequency dependence of the AC quantum Hall resistance was observed on the plateau i=2 for frequencies ranging from 800 Hz to 5 kHz. The frequency coefficient, and the current dependence of R/sub H/ which depend on potentials applied to the back-gates, can simultaneously be reduced to zero. More interestingly, it is also shown that, by removing these back-gates, the losses are considerably reduced giving a negligible frequency coefficient on the order of (0.006/spl plusmn/0.030) (/spl mu//spl Omega///spl Omega/)/kHz.

articleTitle: The analysis of the stability of high DC current comparator with double magnetic detector
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In this paper, for the first time, modeling and simulating for a double magnetic detector dc comparator, based on curvilinear approach and Simulink in MATLAB, are developed. The stability is analyzed. The results show that the double magnetic detector dc comparator has a more perfect stability than the traditional comparator.

articleTitle: Two ions in one trap: ultra-high precision mass spectrometry?
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: By simultaneously trapping two different ions in a Penning trap, we compared their cyclotron frequencies (whose ratio gives their atomic mass ratio) with a precision of about 10/sup -11/ in only a few hours. Unfortunately we observed large abrupt changes in the ratio for which we do not have an explanation.

articleTitle: Design of an SET current meter
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We designed a double integration type current meter as an application of the single electron effect. A single electron pump provides a current source as an inner reference. The potential in between the source and a capacitor is sensed by a single electron electrometer. By switching sources, a current is measured from the ratio of integration times.

articleTitle: Cesium-133 magneto-optical trap at CENAM
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: With the aim of developing a cold cesium atom primary frequency standard, a cesium-133 magneto-optical trap (MOT) has been developed at CENAM's Time and Frequency Division. In this paper we present and discuss the main components of the MOT: the optical, vacuum, and mechanical systems.

articleTitle: Electronic system for increasing the accuracy of in-service instrument-current transformers
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An electronic compensator of ratio errors and phase-displacements is proposed for in-service transformers. Neither an auxiliary winding nor auxiliary core is needed; and large variations of the load connected to the secondary winding are permitted, as it is required by the standards.

articleTitle: Plateaux flatness in the ACQHR: do gates really help?
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We describe audiofrequency measurements of quantum Hall resistors mounted with and without back-gates. When appropriate potentials are applied to the gates, flat plateaux are obtained; but under these circumstances we find ambiguities in the measured Hall values.

articleTitle: Determination of standard resistor temperature coefficients
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Theoretical expressions for resistor temperature coefficients α and β and their uncertainties, as a function of the measurement points, are calculated. An expanded version, where the resistance value R(T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ref</sub>) is included in the fit together with α and β, is also derived. Two different approaches are discussed and compared.

articleTitle: AC voltage converter module with thin-film Multijunction Thermal Converter
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An ac module for a dc multimeter has been designed around the Planar Multijunction Thermal Converter (PMJTC) to measure ac voltage by automatic ac-dc transfer for frequencies from 10 Hz up to 1 MHz. The electronic uses the standard PMJTC in an isothermal way. It applies the sum of the ac signal and the dc feedback at the same time directly to one heater. The dc therefore is an accurate measure for the ac quantity. With this design the time for an accurate ac-dc transfer is reduced considerably.

articleTitle: A compact heterodyne refractometer at 633 nm
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present the results obtained with a compact heterodyne refractometer at 633 nm based on the measurement of the frequency of a laser diode locked to a Fabry Perot cavity, by comparison with a He-Ne laser. An agreement with Edlen's formulas has been obtained at the level of 4/spl times/10/sup -8/, limited by the accuracy of these formulas. The principle of this instrument is similar to the refractometer already developed in our laboratory and working at 780 nm (N. Khelifa et al, Appl. Opt., vol. 37, pp. 156-161, 1998). This apparatus may be also used as an air wavelength reference as described in ref. (R. Thibout et al, Eur. Phys. J. AP., vol. 16, pp. 239-245, 2001).
