This may in some cases also include the cover art, table of contents, copyright statements, title-page or half title-pages, blank pages, venue maps or other general information relating to the conference that was part of the original conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: A re-evaluation of NPL coaxial bridge systems used in the realization of the SI farad via the DC QHE
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A re-evaluation of the coaxial bridge systems used in the traceable measurements of NPL 10 pF primary capacitance standard via the DC, QHE is discussed. Comparisons are made between the previously reported measurement uncertainties and recent measurements on the 100:1 equal power, quadrature, and 10:1 coaxial bridge systems, in order to evaluate systematic errors.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the molar volume of silicon crystals for a determination of the Avogadro constant
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: For a determination of the Avogadro constant N/sub A/ by the X-ray crystal density (XRCD) method, the molar volume M//spl rho/ of three different silicon crystals, NRLM1, NRLM2, and NRLM4, have been analyzed systematically by measurements of their densities /spl rho/ and molar masses M. Details on the sample preparations and the result of measurement are presented.

articleTitle: Cryogenic current comparator designed for current dependence measurement of 1 /spl Omega/ resistor up to 1 A and for superconducting current measurement
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We developed a cryogenic current comparator, to which currents of up to 1 A can be supplied. It was designed to be used for a resistance ratio bridge to measure current dependence of a 1 /spl Omega/ resistor from 50 mA to 1 A by comparing it to a 100 /spl Omega/ resistor with small power coefficiency. It was also designed to be inserted in a superconducting coil to measure superconducting current.

articleTitle: A blind identification technique for the characterization of high voltage impulse measuring systems by means of Kalman filtering
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new technique based on blind identification has been developed for the dynamic characterization of high voltage impulse measuring systems. It is formulated in terms of the extended Kalman filter and, in contrast with existing methods, it allows the identification of the dynamic performance in similar conditions to those of normal operation, i.e., at high voltage level.

articleTitle: Determination of the frequency dependence of capacitance standards with ceramic dielectrics
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The procedure for determination of the frequency dependence (FD) of ceramic capacitance standards characteristic is developed. It is based on application of air capacitance standards with calculable FD, a special summation device and a step calibration method. Measuring instruments are used that allow to compare the capacitance of single capacitors with nominally equal sum capacitance of their combinations. FD of ceramic capacitance standards are determined in the range 100 pF-1 /spl mu/F at frequencies from 50 Hz to 1 MHz. The measurement uncertainty is 0.01-0.1% (k=2).

articleTitle: A precise ccc bridge for QHR standard at NIM
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A ccc bridge was completed in 2000 with uncertainties of several parts in 10/sup 9/ for comparison of QHR to 100 /spl Omega/ or 100 /spl Omega/ to 1 /spl Omega/. Then a bilateral comparison of 1 /spl Omega/ resistors with ETL of Japan was carried out and only a difference of 1.3 n/spl Omega/ was found.

articleTitle: The international comparison of the DC high voltage and AC voltage ratio standards between VNIIMS and UKRCSM
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The results of the international comparison of the DC high voltage and AC voltage ratio standards which were made in the frame of COOMET Project 203/UA/00 between UkrCSM (Ukraine) and VNIIMS (Russia) in June, 2000 in Kyiv are given below.

articleTitle: The VNIIM Josephson junction array voltage standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes the work done at VNIIM, Russia, to establish a voltage standard based on an array of Josephson junctions. The system is described and the results obtained with the system are presented.

articleTitle: The Si-route to the Avogadro constant: new measurements of the molar volume and lattice parameter in an integrated international approach
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: New measurements of the molar volume and lattice parameter of Si, in near-perfect Si crystals, are reported and discussed. These measurements have been planned and performed within a worldwide collaboration coordinated by the CCM working group on the Avogadro constant. The present determination of the molar volume, does confirm the value published previously within stated uncertainty.

articleTitle: The METAS watt balance: a summary of progress
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The Swiss Federal Office of Metrology and Accreditation (METAS) has been continuing its drive towards a 100 g watt balance apparatus with a relative standard uncertainty of 1/spl times/10/sup -8/. The objective of this kind of measurement is, presently, to measure the Planck constant and improve the consistency of the SI. In the future it is hoped that the watt balance approach will help in a redefinition of the kilogram. Currently the experiment is producing preliminary measurements reproducible at the 1 ppm level. Our progress, measurements, and plans for the future are presented.

articleTitle: Stability and accuracy results with the ON/METAS continuous cesium fountain
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The construction of a primary frequency standard based on a continuous beam of laser cooled cesium atoms has been completed. The device is operational and undergoes its first accuracy evaluation. The paper presents stability measurements and accuracy issues, with a special emphasis on the uncertainty contributions that differ from a pulsed fountain.

articleTitle: An improved technique for space charge distribution measurements in solid dielectrics
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A newly developed numerical analysis technique based on inverse matrix calculations is described. It is used to de-convolute electric current waveforms into the space charge and electric field distributions after subjecting solid dielectric samples to a thermal step and measuring the current induced in the external circuit by the perturbation of space charges in the material due to the heat flow. The technique gives significantly lower errors and requires less computation time than commonly used Fourier analysis.

articleTitle: Cs and Rb fountains
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We discuss the present performance and limits of our Cs and Rb fountains. BNM-SYRTE operates three cold atom microwave fountains: two Cs fountains and a dual Cs-Rb fountain. By using an ultra-stable cryogenic sapphire oscillator to probe the atoms, the frequency stability reaches 3.5 /spl times/ 10/sup -14//spl tau//sup -1/2/ which will allow an improvement of the accuracy below the present 10/sup -15/. We discuss here the problems to be solved for reaching a 10/sup -16/ accuracy. We also use the fountains to test the stability of the fine structure constant. Measurements of the ratio v/sub Rb//v/sub Cs/ spread over a two year interval show no change of a at the 7 /spl times/ 10/sup -15//year level.

articleTitle: The magnet assembly in the METAS watt balance experiment
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The permanent magnet of the METAS watt balance is one of the key components of the experiment. Its properties and behavior during the different phases of the experiment must be fully characterized. The importance of thermal and magnetic behavior due to weighing current has been extensively studied with the present design.

articleTitle: Development of a cesium atomic fountain frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report on the development of a cesium atomic fountain frequency standard at KRISS. We have recently observed Ramsey fringes of 1 Hz linewidth on the 9.2 GHz clock transition of cesium atoms in our fountain.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the synchronous generation and synchronous sampling technique for the determination of low frequency AC quantities
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The synchronous synthesis and synchronous measurement of sinusoidal signals using a single internal clock frequency of a high-resolution digitizer as proposed by Ramm et al (IEEE Trans. Instrum. Meas. vol. 48, no. 2, pp. 422-426, 1999) allow the determination of electrical alternating current (AC) quantities (root mean square or RMS values, ratios and power) with unprecedented low uncertainties of the order of /spl mu/V/V and /spl mu/W/W. Extensive theoretical modeling of a system using this technique was done (W.G. Kurten Ihlenfeld, PTB Report E-75, 2001, and PTB Report E-76, 2001). Comparisons to validate the models are shown.

articleTitle: A new architecture for high-accuracy admittance measuring systems
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The architecture of traditional coaxial systems for highly accurate admittance comparison has been redesigned taking into account the features of active-compensated multi-coaxial connection structures previously developed and investigated. When applied to the conventional two-port transformer bridge, the new approach makes the parasitic cable effects negligible, and allows comparison of four-port standards even in parallel connection.

articleTitle: Low-frequency ac-dc voltage transfer standards with new high sensitivity and low power coefficient thin-film Multijunction Thermal Converters
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: New Planar Multijunction Thermal Converters (PMJTC) with low power coefficient and high dynamic range using CuNi44/BiSbTe-thermocouples were developed. Together with carefully evaluated range resistors for voltages up to 1000 V they resulted in ac-dc transfer standards with negligible ac-dc voltage transfer difference at low frequencies. The measuring system was improved with a new highly stable low frequency voltage source.

articleTitle: Interlaboratory comparison using a transport Josephson voltage standard system
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A portable Josephson voltage standard (JVS) system has been used as a transfer standard to make an interlaboratory JVS comparison. The results are compared with an interlaboratory comparison between the same two JVS systems using transport Zeners made at about the same time. The portable JVS improves the uncertainty of the comparison by largely eliminating the problem associated with non-ideal Zener transportability, environmental dependence, and non-linear drift.

articleTitle: Improvements in AC-DC voltage transfer at CENAM
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: At CENAM Mexico, new AC-DC voltage transfer standards have been developed for the voltage range from 2 mV to 1000 V in close cooperation with NMi-VSL, The Netherlands and PTB, Germany. CENAM has improved its measurement techniques and facilities and has participated in international comparisons with PTB, NIST and NRC.

articleTitle: Wavelet-based measurement and classification of power quality disturbances
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper introduces a wavelet-based method for detecting, localizing, quantifying and classifying short duration power quality disturbances. It can take the fast dyadic scheme not the time consuming shift-invariant scheme. Novel binary features are defined and extracted from time or WT domain, and then a simple binary-decimal conversion is sufficient for classification purpose. This benefits the method in both speed and accuracy.

articleTitle: First steps towards a quantum capacitance standard at METAS
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In the 5th framework program of the European Commission, several Metrology Institutes have teamed up in a project (COUNT) aimed at the realization of a primary standard of capacitance based on single electron resistive pumps. In this paper, we report the first steps towards the realization of such a quantum capacitance standard at METAS. The measurement setup is described and the stability diagram of the electron pump, measured at an electronic temperature of 160 mK, is shown. These preliminary results are promising for the future of the experiment.

articleTitle: CO laser for precision frequency measurements in the mid infrared
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Novel features in the design of a CW CO laser are described. The laser system allows selection of a large number of individual laser frequencies with sufficient stability to be used in precise frequency interval measurements in the 50 THz range. This system will be used to bridge the frequency gap between the NRC strontium ion standard and a stabilized commercial 1.5 /spl mu/m laser.

articleTitle: Direct-reading absolute calibration of ac voltage ratio standards
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new system for ac voltage ratio absolute calibration has been developed at IEN. The voltage ratio is maintained with a new one-decade, two-stage inductive voltage divider. The setup for ratio self-calibration is based on the simplest possible application of the bootstrap method: during the step-up the voltage differences are directly read with a vector voltmeter having an extremely high ac common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR).

articleTitle: Impedance correction of one-port coaxial loads using reference air line
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An impedance measurement method for one-port coaxial load using multiple reference air lines as the impedance standard and offset open and short as the reflection standard is presented in this paper. Measured impedances for termination and sliding load are presented and the measurement uncertainty is evaluated.

articleTitle: Role of acoustical reflections in quantised acousto-electric current devices
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In surface acoustic wave devices exhibiting quantised acoustoelectric current (QAC) transport, the precision of quantisation, which is crucial in a potential application as a current standard, is influenced by reflections of the acoustic wave. We studied the role of these reflections in two extreme limits: an intentionally applied counterpropagating SAW beam simulates intense reflections, whereas a nearly reflectionless situation is realised with a specially designed device. In contrast to previous findings, we conclude that acoustic echoes are always detrimental and should be avoided completely.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of a diode-pumped Nd:YAG laser at 532 nm to iodine by using third-harmonic technique
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A compact frequency standard was constructed by stabilizing the frequency of a diode-pumped Nd:YAG laser to the Doppler-free spectrum of iodine at 532 nm. The results show that by using standard third-harmonic locking technique good stability can be achieved in a relatively small, simple and inexpensive set-up.

articleTitle: Improving the mechanical stability of a standard capacitor
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: CSIR-NML-manufactured 10 pF ULE (Ultra-Low Expansion) quartz capacitors had been in use since the early 1970's. Although the capacitors were extremely stable, they were susceptible to mechanical shock. We present the development of a standard capacitor, with improvements to increase its robustness as well as results of shock and vibration tests.

articleTitle: Optimization of AC power measurements for immunity to spectral leakage due to imperfect phase-locking
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Power measurements can benefit from spectral analysis. It may, however, also lead to errors that are not immediately recognizable, caused by spectral leakage due to imperfect phase-locking in measurement systems. This paper analyses this problem for low-frequency AC power measurements. The conclusion is that if any spectral decomposition is made, care should be taken not to use excessive measurement times, and that the phase-locked loop bandwidth should be kept as low as possible.

articleTitle: Remeasurement of the (220) lattice spacing of silicon
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A need arose for a reduction of the present relative uncertainty in the measurement of the silicon lattice spacing down to 10/sup -9/. This paper describes our advances towards this goal.

articleTitle: Simplified calculus for the design of a cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The calculation of inductances of superconducting structures like the cryogenic current comparator (CCC) is not straightforward due to image effects. We have found a "rule of thumb" that maximizes the value of an inductance inside a superconducting shield. With this rule, the design of an optimum CCC is simplified.

articleTitle: Sub-5-ps electrical pulses for the characterization of high-frequency components
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Presents a method that allows one to launch 3.3 (4.9) ps voltage pulses into coaxial (coplanar) transmission lines. With this technique, high frequency-components can be characterized at frequencies well above 100 GHz.

articleTitle: Comparison of independent optical frequency measurements using a portable I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG laser
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An international comparison of two independent absolute optical frequency measurements between NMIJ/AIST, Japan and JILA, USA has been made using a portable Nd:YAG laser. The agreement between the two measurements is 330/spl plusmn/380 Hz, yielding a measurement uncertainty of 6.7/spl times/10/sup -13/ that is mainly contributed from the reproducibility of the portable laser. This comparison is used to confirm the measured absolute frequency of NMIJ-Y3, which is reported to the Consultative Committee for Length (CCL) for the determination of the frequency value of iodine-stabilized Nd:YAG lasers.

articleTitle: The CIPM MRA in its 3/sup rd/ year of implementation in Europe
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Since the signing of the CIPM MRA in October 1999 the world's metrology community is implementing this unique and far-reaching arrangement. This presentation, in the middle of the transitional period of four years, highlights the processes, the current status and the future of the MRA in EUROMET.

articleTitle: Effective cw frequency tripling of cooling laser for magnesium ions
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Frequency tripling of cw 840 nm laser is obtained for laser cooling of magnesium ions. This beam at 280 nm is expected to improve the long-term and short-term stability of optical frequency standard by laser-cooled ions. Our frequency conversion system is essentially applicable to other wavelength.

articleTitle: Development of a 1.5 micron acetylene stabilised frequency standard and the measurement of its frequency using single Sr/sup +/ standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report progress on the development of an optical frequency standard at 1.5 micron referenced to rovibrational transitions in acetylene. This work not only yields a frequency reference of relevance to precision physical measurements, but also addresses the near term need for 100 kHz-1 MHz accuracy in calibration procedures for dense WDM optical communication systems. Absolute frequency measurements of a tuneable diode laser stabilized on the acetylene saturated-absorption lines are being carried out using a link to the accurate NRC single ion reference.

articleTitle: Femtosecond optical frequency comb measurements at NPL
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Absolute frequency measurements of optical frequency standards are being made at NPL using a femtosecond optical frequency comb referenced to a hydrogen maser. In particular, measurement of a transportable methane-stabilized helium-neon laser system provides a test of the femtosecond comb at the few parts in 10/sup 13/ level.

articleTitle: EUROMET comparisons of the SMU Josephson array voltage standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A comparisons of the 10 V Josephson array voltage standard (JAVS) of the Slovak Institute of Metrology (SMU, Bratislava, Slovakia) was carried out in the framework of two EUROMET projects no. 496 and 497. The Zener diode-based transfer standards have been used for all comparisons, the results of which are presented in this contribution.

articleTitle: Optical frequency measurement and standards
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. The last three years have seen the rapid fruition of the long-standing dream in which we can easily and accurately measure optical frequencies. This capability has matured so powerfully that papers are beginning to appear with the words "Optical Clock" in their titles. The in-principle advantages of optical transitions regarding line-Q also are appearing in real systems, although some challenges arise from the complexity of operating simultaneously with laser atomic cooling AND optical frequency stabilization AND accurate frequency measurement. An interesting avenue for practical clocks, albeit with some reduction of accuracy-capability, is possible with gas cells. For example, using molecular iodine's visible transitions, performance superior to 1/spl times/10/sup 14/ at 1 s should be obtained with a variant of NICE-OHMS spectroscopy at 532 nm. Recent advances in controlling to sub-10 ppm levels the Residual Amplitude Modulation of the Electro-Optic Phase Modulator should lead to frequency repeatability at the range of a few Hz (/spl sim/1/spl times/10/sup -14/).

articleTitle: Comparison CCEM-K8: final evaluation of the travelling standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Circulation of the travelling standard for international comparison CCEM-K8 on DC voltage ratio was completed in June 2001. Awaiting the conclusion of the process leading to the agreed final report, the final evaluation of the behavior of the standard is given.

articleTitle: Results from international comparisons at the BIPM providing a world wide reference network of /sup 127/I/sub 2/-stabilized frequency-doubled Nd:YAG lasers
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. Frequency comparisons of iodine-stabilized Nd:YAG lasers from the BIPM, the BNM-INM, the CMI, the MIKES, and the NMIJ/AIST have been made. The frequencies of these lasers can now be linked together with those of absolutely measured lasers from the JILA/NIST, the PTB and the ILP (Novosibirsk).

articleTitle: Narrow-linewidth Nd:YAG laser for the single indium ion optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. Using active vibration isolation of a high-finesse reference cavity, we demonstrate a Hz-level linewidth of a 946 nm laser, used for high-resolution spectroscopy of the indium ion clock transition. Recent experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Determination of voltage coefficient of high DC voltage resistor
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A binary step-up method to determine the voltage coefficient of high dc voltage resistor has been developed. Range of voltage and accuracy of measurement depends only on stabilities of the high voltage source and the resistor under measurement. Rough measurement of 100 M/spl Omega/ resistor shows an uncertainty less than 100 /spl Omega//kV up to 50 kV.

articleTitle: Formation and distortions of the ultrashort pulse train spectrum broadened in tapered fiber
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We propose a theoretical description and give experimental results of the ultrashort pulse train spectral broadening in tapered fibers. A multi-peak spectral structure due to the effect of self-phase modulation was obtained. Phase and amplitude fluctuations were investigated. It is shown that stability of intermode beats remains after propagation through the tapered fiber.

articleTitle: Deternunation of the high-voltage dependence of fluke 792A at NIM
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes a method of using inductive voltage divider (ND) to determine the voltage dependence of voltage ac-dc transfer standard of Fluke 792A at voltage above 200 V and at frequencies of 50 kHz and 100 Wz. The evaluation of the voltage dependence of the ratio ermr of IVD and the test set-up are described and the preliminary results are repotted.

articleTitle: A beam balance experiment to determine the gravitational constant
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The goal of our experiment is a precision measurement of the gravitational constant G by means of a beam balance. The gravitational forces of two large and movable field masses act on test masses and change their weights. First measurements have been successfully completed with a relative uncertainty of 230 ppm. Since then various upgrades and improvements have been implemented.

articleTitle: Reduction of microwave attenuation in superconducting microstripline using plasma nitridation
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have been developed a new fabrication process of Josephson junction series array (JJA) by using reactive ion etching (RIE) and a self-aligning technique. A plasma nitridation process is also employed in improving the microwave transmission characteristics by blocking the O/sub 2/ from diffusing into the Nb ground-plane by depositing SiO/sub 2/ dielectric layer using plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) at substrate temperature of 300/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Uncertainties of impulse voltage measurements at NML, CSIRO and INMS, NRC
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes high voltage impulse measurements made under the controlled conditions of a calibration in national measurement laboratories to establish the best agreement that could be achieved in comparison measurements on small reference resistor dividers.

articleTitle: Iodine stabilized dye laser system for traceable calibration of secondary wavelength standard HeNe lasers
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A dye laser system tuneable from 540 nm to 670 nm and stabilized to reference iodine saturated absorption resonances is described. The current system allows traceable calibration of a number of visible and near IR HeNe reference frequencies. Evaluation of the system's stability and accuracy were obtained via a heterodyne intercomparison with a NRC 633 nm iodine stabilized HeNe laser.

articleTitle: Application of six-port wave-correlator for very low velocity measurement using Doppler effect
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new technique is proposed for measuring the Doppler frequency of a moving object by using the six-port correlator. The examination of this new proposal has been done with an object moving at a very low speed. The experiment and simulation results show the target velocity around 0.2 mm/s has been successfully inferred, which proved the validity of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: VNA calibration by random neural network
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new calibration method is investigated for conventional VNA calibration. It is based on teaching the error terms of VNA to a Neural Network (NN). A well-known two ports calibration standard is adequate VNA calibration for this method. Experimental results are presented and compared to data obtained with traditional techniques.

articleTitle: Design of a cold atom source for a neutral strontium optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We discuss the design of a cold atom source for a neutral strontium optical frequency standard. The cooling laser light at 461 nm is produced by sum frequency generation by a KTP crystal inside a doubly resonant cavity. Up to 120 mW of blue light are generated. We also describe the atomic beam and the Zeeman slower from which the atoms are captured.

articleTitle: A microwave frequency standard based on laser-cooled /sup 171/Yb/sup +/ ions
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report operation of a microwave frequency standard based on the 12.6 GHz ground-state hyperfine transition in a cloud of laser-cooled /sup 171/Yb/sup +/ ions. The projected performance of this standard (frequency uncertainty /spl les/ 4 /spl times/ 10/sup -15/ and stability 5 /spl times/ 10/sup -14/ /spl tau//sup -1/2/ for a 10 s Ramsey time) is comparable to that of a cesium fountain.

articleTitle: Characterisation of SINIS programmable Josephson arrays at Justervesenet
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Justervesenet (JV) have developed two set-ups for programmable Josephson arrays. One set-up for arrays operating up to 20 GHz and one for frequencies from 72.5 GHz to 76 GHz. The set-ups and results from the characterisation of three different programmable arrays of the intrinsically shunted SINIS type are presented. The arrays were a /spl sim/20 mV array with 512 junctions binary divided into 8 segments operating from 10 GHz to 20 GHz and two 1 volt arrays operating at 72.5 to 76 GHz with 8192 junctions binary divided into 14 and 6 segments. All arrays were manufactured by the Physicalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) in Germany.

articleTitle: Analysis of lattice-strain effects in LLL X-ray interferometers by Takagi equations
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The Takagi approach has been used to study whether the determination of the Si lattice parameter a/sub o/, with 10/sup -9/ relative uncertainty, is affected by lattice strains of various kind.

articleTitle: Density comparison measurements of silicon crystals by pressure of flotation method
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Since silicon single crystals are believed to be the most perfect crystals to be obtained at the present time, they are used for the density standard and the determination of the Avogadro constant. However, there exists molar volume discrepancies among them. It is thought that the problems exist in the degree of perfection of the silicon crystal. It is important, therefore, to study defect and impurity effects on the density of silicon in order to clarify the cause of the discrepancies. We have developed a density comparison measurement system based on the pressure of flotation method (PFM). Density differences for silicon spheres produced from a new FZ-silicon ingot of NRLM4 was measured. The second generation of this PFM apparatus is being installed in the National Metrology Institute of Japan (NMIJ).

articleTitle: Accuracy assessment of analysis of a free-fall gravimeter data
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: In absolute gravity measurements, a laser interferometer tracks the motion of a free falling retroreflector. The value of the local acceleration due to gravity is obtained by timing the traveling interference fringes. This paper presents the accuracy assessment of digital fringe processing for the extraction of gravity value from the digitized data.

articleTitle: Behaviour and frequency dependence of AC-DC high voltage transfer standard under humidity step changes
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Under humidity step changes, the measured AC-DC difference results from a thermal converter and a range resistor at 200 V in the frequency range from 40 Hz to 100 kHz have shown that a first order differential equation can be used to model the behaviour. The humidity coefficients for the model are found to be strongly frequency-dependent and the time constants are related to the changes in humidity.

articleTitle: Production of raman laser beams using injection-locking technique
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We produced two Raman-laser beams with a frequency offset of 9.2-GHz using a simple injection-locking technique. A slave diode-laser is injection-locked to one f first-order sidebands of a master diode-laser produced by a 9.2 GHz EOM (electro-optic modulator). Using these Raman-laser beams, we observed CPT resonance in a cesium vapor cell.

articleTitle: A traceable precision current source for currents between 100 aA and 10 pA
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present a new traceable calibration source for small currents in the range from 100 aA to 10 pA. An extremely stable output current is achieved by use of a newly developed precision voltage ramp generator.

articleTitle: Calorimetric measurements on losses in superconducting materials
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We are constructing a cryogenic dual compensated calorimeter for loss measurements in superconducting materials. We plan to measure the losses due to the incomplete Meissner effect in slowly varying small magnetic fields appropriate for levitation. These measurements bear importance for the realization of the kilogram using the superconducting magnetic levitation method.

articleTitle: Thrust measurement at micronewton level
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An interferometric force balance (Nanobalance) for space micro-thruster qualification is presented. A new generation of space micro-thrusters is under development aiming at thrust resolution and accuracy below one micronewton. Nanobalance has been conceived and developed for ground calibration of thrust time profile and noise with sub-micronewton accuracy.

articleTitle: Volume of the Avogadro sphere: diameter determination with the spheres interferometer
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: For the new determination of Avogadro's constant, N/sub A/, one part of the measuring task consists in the high accuracy determination of the volume of a silicon sphere with a mass of 1 kg and a diameter of about 90 mm. An interferometer with spherical reference surfaces has been designed for this specific purpose. The measuring principle of the interferometer and first measurements on silicon spheres are described.

articleTitle: Analytic result for corrections of order /spl alpha/(z/spl alpha/)/sup 5/(m/M)m to Lamb shift
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The results and main steps of an analytic calculation of radiative-recoil corrections of order /spl alpha/(Z/spl alpha/)/sup 5/(m/M)m to the Lamb shift in hydrogen are presented. The calculations are performed in the infrared safe Yennie gauge. The discrepancy between two previous numerical calculations of these corrections existing in the literature is resolved. Our result eliminates the largest source of the theoretical uncertainty in the magnitude of the deuterium-hydrogen isotope shift.

articleTitle: Research of long-time stability of an atomic magnetic resonance standard system for reproduction of direct current and magnetic flux density
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: At the D. I. Mendeleyev Institute for Metrology (VNIIM) a standard system using helium-4 atomic magnetic resonance has operated during the past 10 years for reproduction of low magnetic flux density and direct current. Research of the base elements of this system for the last 5 years have shown that non-stability of the coil-constant of a standard solenoid and nonlinearity of the frequency-to-current conversion coefficient of a quantum system for current reproduction in the range 0.1 A to 1 A are less than 1 /spl times/ 10/sup -7/.

articleTitle: A precision set-up and method for calibrating a DC voltage divider's ratios from 10 V to 1000 V
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A precision set-up and method for calibrating the division ratios of a resistive divider for DC-voltage in the range 10 V to 1000 V is described. The method requires equipment commonly available in most standard laboratories. Uncertainties better than 3/spl times/10/sup -7/ (k = 2) in the ratio is achieved.

articleTitle: Remarks on high precision multimeter calibration
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Digital multimeters (DMMs) are a widely used electrical measurement instrument. Strategy of DMM calibration is described in EA-10/15. This paper discusses additional test of linearity resistance measurement. A possible systematic error of calibration of AC voltage function when the calibrator used was calibrated with thermal AC/DC standard is also covered.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a new 10 mA DC current reference standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new DC current reference standard has been developed as a component in a current calibration hierarchy in the LHC project at CERN. The standard provides 10 mA DC current with an accuracy <0.5 ppm, drift <2 ppm/year and compliance error <0.1 ppm for 0-10 V. The paper gives the results from two years evaluation of a series of 5 units.

articleTitle: Improvements of measuring system on magnetic levitation system for the determination of magnetic flux quantum
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A development of a video frame synchronized data sampling system is in progress for superconducting magnetic levitation system parameters to correct an error of vertical displacement reading due to attitude change of floating body using real time movement analysis in equilibrium condition.

articleTitle: Temperature characteristic of Zener reference standards
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We investigated temperature dependencies of Zener-diode voltage reference standards. Some Zeners showed output voltage differences between ac line power and battery operation, and the voltage differences were related to the oven temperature change in the Zeners. A waiting time of five hours was suggested when the Zener was operated by the battery.

articleTitle: Temperature stability improvement of on-chip reference elements using integrated Peltier coolers
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: On-chip integrated Peltier coolers have potential for the thermal control and stabilisation of highly localised sections of a silicon integrated circuit, at a minimum possible temperature. In an on-chip reference this ensures improved stability, without reducing basic device operation. This paper emphasises the experimental characterisation and, in a later stage, validation thereof. Initial results show a figure-of-merit of 0.26/spl middot/10/sup -3/ K/sup -1/, while a temperature drop of 2.1 K can be established.

articleTitle: Measurement of h/MRb with ultracold atoms
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We present the development of a new experiment with ultracold atoms. Its purpose is to measure the atomic recoil frequency shift of photons absorbed or emitted by an atom. One can deduce the ratio h/M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Rb</sub> Rb between the Planck constant and the mass of the atom, leading to the determination of the fine structure constant (α).

articleTitle: A voltage device used as high accurate voltage ratio standard
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A voltage device based on connecting the voltage units in series-parallel configuration is proposed in this paper. It is similar to the well-known Hamon device (B.V. Hamon, J. Sci. Instr., vol. 31, pp. 450-453, 1954). It can be used to transfer the voltage to its multiple units for calibration of the voltage standard. This type of voltage device can also be used as the proportional arms of a voltage proportional bridge for obtaining the proportional transformation with high accuracy.

articleTitle: DC voltage divider calibration system at NMIJ
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A system to calibrate DC voltage divider with increment taps up to 1 kV has been developed. During calibration, the divider is grounded and driving current is supplied, similarly to when used after being calibrated. Relative combined uncertainty of 1000 V/10 V was 0.1 parts per million (k = 1).

articleTitle: Stability of silicon microfabricated pull-in voltage references
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Micromechanical structures have been designed, fabricated in silicon and tested for use as on-chip voltage reference. Applications are in electrical metrology and in integrated silicon microsystems. Microbeams of 100 /spl mu/m length, 3 /spl mu/m width and 11 /spl mu/m thickness are electrostatically actuated with a very reproducible pull-in voltage at 9.1 V. Devices demonstrated an initial drift of -12 mV over 10 days and stabilised with a 500 /spl mu/V uncertainty. The temperature coefficient is 1.2 mV/K and the overall noise level is at 100 /spl mu/V (analytical value).

articleTitle: Linking the results of 10 pF capacitance key comparisons CCEM-K4 and EUROMET 345
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We propose a method to link the results of two 10 pF capacitance key comparisons: CCEM-K4 and EUROMET Project 345. The link is made through the results of six linking laboratories who participated in both comparisons. The outcome is two-fold: estimates of the degrees of equivalence with respect to the CCEM key comparison reference value (KCRV) for those laboratories who participated in the EUROMET comparison only, and a matrix giving the bilateral degrees of equivalence for all pairs of laboratories.

articleTitle: An improved BIPM torsion-strip balance for determining G
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Reports progress of a programme to measure the Newtonian constant of gravitation, G, with a torsion strip balance using several different methods. We have recently published a result with an uncertainty of 41 parts per million (ppm). The present efforts are aimed at reducing this uncertainty to about 10 ppm.

articleTitle: Test for the time independence of the fine structure constant, /spl alpha/, using cryogenic sapphire resonators at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new experiment to test for the time independence of the fine structure constant, /spl alpha/, is proposed. The experiment utilizes different polarized modes in a sapphire resonator. When configured as a dual mode sapphire clock, we show that it is possible to undertake a sensitive measurement from the beat frequency between the two modes.

articleTitle: Polarization contributions of order /spl alpha//sup 2/(Z/spl alpha/)(m/M)E/sub F/ to hyperfine splitting in muonium
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We calculate radiative-recoil corrections of order /spl alpha//sup 2/(Z/spl alpha/)(m/M)E/sub F/ to hyperfine splitting in muonium generated by the diagrams with electron and muon polarization loops. The single-logarithmic and nonlogarithmic contributions calculated here improve the theory of hyperfine splitting, and affect the value of the electron-muon mass ratio extracted from the experimental data on the muonium hyperfine splitting.

articleTitle: Analyses of frequency stability and operating parameters of caesium clocks over the entire life span
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper presents the results of life-long monitoring of the operating parameters and frequency stability of two HP5071A caesium clocks with high performance tubes. More data is available to support the analyses reported in our previous paper (ATF2000, pp. 179-186, 2000).

articleTitle: Electroluminescence - an optical technique to determine the early stages of polymer degradation under high electric stresses
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An experimental setup to detect electroluminescence (EL) in polymeric dielectric subjected to high electric stresses is described. The technique, which is at least three orders of magnitude more sensitive than conventional partial discharge detection systems, shows that the spectra of EL are in the visible and ultraviolet ranges and could cause polymer degradation.

articleTitle: Population relaxation of Cs atoms in MOT [frequency standard applications]
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The dynamical behavior of magneto-optically trapped (MOT) Cs atoms is studied by a laser-spectroscopic method. Atoms in the region irradiated by a pulsed laser beam are ejected from the MOT. Recovery of the local population appears in the absorption signals of a probe laser while total population is observed as a fluorescence signal. Anomalously large absorption is observed just after the pulse irradiation.

articleTitle: Measuring resistance standards in terms of the quantised Hall resistance with a dual Josephson voltage standard using SINIS Josephson arrays
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Based on a dual Josephson voltage standard, a measuring system has been set up for highly precise determinations of resistance ratios. It is demonstrated that, by means of this system, 10-k/spl Omega/ and 100-/spl Omega/ standard resistors can be linked to a 12.9-k/spl Omega/ quantised Hall resistance with expanded uncertainties (k=2) of 5 parts in 10/sup 9/ and 20 parts in 10/sup 9/, respectively.

articleTitle: The resistance standard based on the quantum Hall effect at Slovak Institute of Metrology
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper describes the resistance standard based on quantum Hall effect and a device for the quantum Hall resistance (QHR) in Slovak Institute of Metrology (SMU). The preliminary results of the 100 /spl Omega/ resistor calibration are presented.

articleTitle: Minimum variance analysis of international comparison data
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An alternative approach, the minimum variance method, is applied to calculate results of international comparisons. Time-dependent estimates of the output of the transfer standard are calculated for each participant, based on the noise properties of the standard. By abandoning the single reference value concept, the method avoids self-correlation and treats the participants equally.

articleTitle: Frequency and current coefficients of the AC quantum Hall resistance
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: It has been shown recently at BIPM and PTB that the AC characteristics of quantum Hall samples can be adjusted by means of gates or windows. Now we present current results of samples without gates or windows, and we discuss whether a similar effect can be obtained.

articleTitle: Using a high-value resistor in single-electron counting measurements
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: An experiment using a high-value cryogenic resistor is proposed, with the aim of improving the experimental link between three quantum electrical standards. This technique is new in its approach and does not require feedback from either a voltage detector or a current detector. Performance is limited by fundamental resistor and SQUID detector noise.

articleTitle: Extension of the IEN traceability for AC voltages below 200 mV
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The system, the standards and the procedures developed at IEN for the extension of the traceability to low voltage ranges down to 1 mV are described. Specific new features are the low voltage generator system, the procedures for building the traceability and the method for the evaluation of the load correction based on perturbations with known admittances.

articleTitle: Precise ratio transformer: a new concept of the magnetic system
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: A new magnetic system has been developed that allows increased eficiency of magnetic core material usage, simplified shielding of windings and a decrease in the length of windings in a precise-ratio transformer. The uncertainty of the voltage ratio can be decreased to the order of IO' in both single- and double-stage variants of the transformer.

articleTitle: Four-port AC quantized Hall resistance measurements
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Measurements of the quantized Hall resistance R/sub H/(i) for i=2 have been made in the frequency range 200 Hz to 2 kHz using a four-port bridge. Some preliminary results are reported.

articleTitle: The segment copper shielding structure in comparators
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The segment copper shielding structure in comparators is discussed. A fire-new segment copper shielding structure which can improve the EMC of comparators is given. The new shielding method mentioned above is applied in comparators designed for on-site test of the output current transforms of AC generators. Its validity is proved.

articleTitle: Progress in the implementation of the capacitance standard based on single-electron counting at PTB
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We report on the progress achieved at PTB in setting up an experiment for the realization of a quantum capacitance standard based on the controlled charging of a capacitor by single electrons. An experiment of this kind was suggested and first performed by NIST. In order to enhance the accuracy of the experiment, we use a new kind of single-electron pump and a capacitor with improved design features. The main components for the experiment are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Thin film designs for 1000V ac range resistors
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Alternatives to the traditional coaxial design of precision ac range resistors have resulted in performance breakthroughs, reducing both ac-dc difference and settling times. Application of thin film resistor technology and innovative thermal design has made these advancements possible.

articleTitle: Progress in measurements of electron pump by means of a CCC
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: This paper deals with the improvements of the experimental setup devoted to high-accuracy measuring of current across the single electron pump carried out at the BNM-LNE (formerly BNM-LCIE). Preliminary results of measurements of current voltage characteristics of the three-junction Cr-Al R-pump fabricated at PTB are given.

articleTitle: Improved IEN cryogenic system for AC-DC transfer in the 1 mV range
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes the design and the development of an improved system for AC-DC transfer measurements in the 1 mV range at cryogenic temperature. A new thermal system has been built. The design of a device with two heaters for application in differential configurations is optimized for a more suitable time constant. A second thermometer in the same chip is used as a sensor for the second stage of the temperature control.

articleTitle: A new transfer device for the NRC Travelling Standard Program
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: The paper describes a measurement system, which is now used as a transfer device for the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) Travelling Standard Program. The system is based on two sampling voltmeters and a computer used for data acquisition and analysis. The equipment is used on-site with an ac source and a new 12-position pulse-frequency comparator to provide traceability for the standards maintained by Canadian electrical utilities and electricity meter manufacturers. The accuracy of the system is better than 30 parts in 10/sup 6/. The repeatability of the errors before and after an on-site calibration is generally better than 15 parts in 10/sup 6/.

articleTitle: Optimization of the precise inductive voltage divider windings
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Ratio errors of inductive voltage dividers (IVDs) can be reduced by using trifilar ropes for the multifilar winding fabrication. Unevenness of distributed parameters of such a multifilar winding does not exceed 10%. Positioning the largest members of mutual capacitances matrix nearby of its main diagonal provides tenfold reduction of an IVD ratio error. The model of inner capacitive load distribution is verified by direct measurements of the rope currents by means of a current comparator.

articleTitle: NRC-NIST intercomparison of calibration systems for current transducers with a voltage output at power frequencies
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. A number of international comparisons of current transformer calibrations at power frequencies were conducted in the past. However, all of them were done with a secondary current output of 5 A. This intercomparison of current transformer calibration systems between the National Research Council of Canada and the National Institute of Standards and Technology, USA, is done with a primary current range of 100 A and a secondary output signal of voltage range of 10 V. The comparison is implemented with a transfer standard consisting of a modified commercial current-comparator-based transimpedance with the output voltage adjustable in magnitude and phase within a range of /spl plusmn/1 percent.

articleTitle: Cotunneling errors in the three-junction R-pump
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: We have investigated the influence of the dissipative circuit impedance on the cotunneling process in a double junction system and on the accuracy of the 3-junction R-pump.

articleTitle: Frequency performance of 12 906 /spl Omega/ and 6 453 /spl Omega/ reference resistors for ac quantum Hall effect experiments: results of a Euromet project
publicationTitle: Conference Digest Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements
abstract: To enable quantifying the degree of equivalence of different ways of measuring quantized Hall resistances, 12 906 /spl Omega/ and 6 453 /spl Omega/ travelling resistors have been prepared and utilized as transfer standards in a comparison based on measurement of their frequency performances at a number of laboratories.
